#2223. Milan, Amorim: "Turnover? Dobbiamo stare molto attenti con alcuni giocatori"

Ruben Amorim, allenatore del Milan, è presente in conferenza stampa, a partire dalle ore 14:00, alla vigilia di Milan-Ferencvaros, sfida valida per la quarta giornata della League Phase di Europa League e in programma domani alle 18.45 a San Siro. Segui in diretta le dichiarazioni del tecnico rossonero con il live testuale su TMW.

Importante mettersi alle spalle il derby... "Sì, bisogna pensare a domani per mantenere questa costanza. Penso che siamo stati costanti durante la partita e ci sono state gare in cui non lo siamo stati, quindi cerchiamo di ripeterci nella prossima sfida. Questo è il grande passo avanti che dobbiamo compiere. Non importa il turnover, non contano i giocatori che mandiamo in campo: dobbiamo essere un'ottima squadra. Dobbiamo vincere domani, perché è fondamentale per il nostro obiettivo di andare fino in fondo in questa competizione".

Turnover? "La partita più importante è domani. Dobbiamo stare molto attenti con alcuni giocatori. Abbiamo alle spalle questo calendario fitto e non possiamo permetterci di perdere molti elementi per le prossime partite, perché a volte, quando non vuoi fare turnover o preservare un po' le gambe, ti ritrovi con un infortunio che ti tiene fuori per un mese o un mese e mezzo. Questa è la partita più importante; stiamo pensando solo a questa, ma dovremo fare un po' di turnover e tutti i ragazzi sono pronti a reggere l'impatto con le richieste della gara. Abbiamo la responsabilità di vincere l'incontro. Affronteremo un grande avversario che ha nove punti in questa competizione, una squadra che non sta perdendo neanche una partita in campionato, ma i nostri calciatori sono pronti e abbiamo il dovere di vincere".

Perché questa differenza di risultati tra Serie A e Europa League? "A volte è difficile da spiegare. Può succedere con il turnover, a volte dobbiamo fare scelte che cambiano un po' il nostro modo di giocare. Ma se poi guardi le partite contro il Benfica, credo che non abbiamo espresso il nostro gioco, pur avendo avuto più possesso palla. Abbiamo avuto qualche problema nelle poche occasioni concesse all'avversario e abbiamo subito gol. Poi abbiamo vinto un'ottima partita a Salisburgo e poi a Bournemouth. Abbiamo avuto un'espulsione, due rigori, è stata colpa nostra. La situazione di Maignan non ci ha aiutati a lottare per la partita, e a volte in certi momenti si verificano queste dinamiche. Credo che non stiamo andando davvero bene in Serie A; naturalmente abbiamo vinto l'ultima, ma guardando la squadra e le partite, penso che dovremmo avere più punti. Quindi non sono soddisfatto in Europa League, non sono soddisfatto in Serie A. Penso che possiamo fare di meglio, ma a volte va così. Ogni partita ha la sua storia. Abbiamo avuto qualche problema in Europa League, ma credo che domani potremo cambiare le cose e vincere la partita."

Ci presenta il Ferencvaros? "Il Ferencvaros è una squadra abituata a vincere e, a prescindere dal contesto, questo ti dà una grande fiducia per affrontare tutte le partite. Sono a loro agio nella posizione in cui si trovano, stanno facendo benissimo in campionato e giocano con un 4-2-3-1, potendo contare su un'ottima rotazione nella rosa. Si percepisce chiaramente un'identità ben definita in quella squadra. Hanno un centrocampista, Nagy, molto bravo a impostare, abbassandosi a costruire la manovra a tre. Hanno un'identità, sanno come giocare, sanno come vincere le partite e sono davvero a loro agio. Vengono a San Siro senza nulla da perdere: l'avversario è abituato a vincere, ma la responsabilità, qui a San Siro, è nostra. Dobbiamo giocare molto bene, essere estremamente concentrati e, come ho detto ai ragazzi, contro l'Inter siamo stati bravi perché siamo stati umili e molto attenti ai dettagli. Dobbiamo avere lo stesso identico atteggiamento contro il Ferencvaros, perché questa è la cosa più importante con una squadra così. Dobbiamo essere concentrati, umili e curare ogni minimo dettaglio per vincere questa partita, perché affrontiamo un avversario forte".

Che partita si aspetta domani? "Posso dirti che possiamo perdere qualsiasi partita, così come possiamo vincere qualsiasi partita. È questa la caratteristica principale di questa squadra, e dipende da come affrontiamo l'impegno. Quindi, non importa se l'avversario arriva dalla Serie A, dalla Serie B, dall'Europa League o dalla Champions League: possiamo vincere con chiunque, ma allo stesso tempo possiamo perdere contro chiunque, soprattutto oggi che tutti conoscono tutti. Ogni giocatore ha gli strumenti e le capacità tecniche, e gli allenatori capiscono l'avversario e dispongono di tutti i video necessari per preparare la gara. Non è solo una questione legata al Ferencvaros: possiamo perdere con chiunque, ma possiamo anche vincere con chiunque. Dipende anche da noi e, a volte, da un pizzico di fortuna".

La squadra ha una sua identità ora? "La nostra identità è sempre chiara. Penso che abbiamo già un'identità. Vogliamo dominare le partite: a volte ci riusciamo, a volte no, ma nella maggior parte delle gare cerchiamo di essere propositivi. Questo è l'inizio della nostra identità. A volte cambiamo il sistema o il modo in cui difendiamo, ma a volte non te ne accorgi nemmeno. Credo che la nostra identità consista nell'essere propositivi in campo e nel cercare di fare la partita. Penso che ci manchi chiaramente la capacità di schiacciare l'avversario vicino alla sua area e di mantenere lì il pallone per creare più occasioni. Credo che questo sia il nostro problema principale, insieme alla costanza durante le partite e nell'arco della stagione. Penso che stiamo migliorando da questo punto di vista, che stiamo giocando meglio per più tratti e che stiamo controllando le gare un po' meglio. Ma se guardo alla squadra, abbiamo ancora tanto lavoro da fare, soprattutto ho questa sensazione quando arriviamo negli ultimi trenta metri: non riusciamo a portare lì la palla e a stazionare stabilmente, ed è qualcosa su cui abbiamo bisogno di tempo per lavorare e in cui devo aiutare i miei giocatori a esprimersi meglio in quel momento".

ll Milan nel derby si è saputo difendere molto bene nel secondo tempo... "Dimostriamo domani che possiamo difendere ancora meglio. Credo che abbiamo controllato bene la partita perché abbiamo avuto più possesso palla. Non si tratta solo di pensare a difendere: noi difendiamo con la palla, e questo ci aiuta a ragionare con più lucidità quando non ce l'abbiamo. Poi penso che siamo stati più bravi nei dettagli. Un metro è un metro: un metro più vicini ai compagni è un metro, non due metri. E su tutti questi piccoli particolari siamo stati superiori rispetto alla partita con Bologna, è questa la sensazione che ho avuto. Siamo stati davvero aggressivi sulle corsie laterali perché sapevamo che, soprattutto con Dimarco, il cross arriva, Esposito è dentro l'area, Thuram è dentro, e non possiamo concedere quei traversoni perché poi diventa una lotteria, un 50 e 50. De Winter è stato straordinario, ma se lasci partire un cross in più verso Thuram, diventa impossibile difendere. Quindi forse è il modo in cui a volte percepiamo l'avversario, ed è un aspetto che dobbiamo cambiare nella nostra testa. Credo che prima di tutto difendiamo bene tenendo palla, e poi senza palla siamo stati più aggressivi, perché sapevamo già che se fosse successo qualcosa, come un cross di Dimarco, poteva succedere l'irreparabile. Dobbiamo gestirla questa situazione. Ed è sempre quello che dico: quando una squadra vince sempre, c'è un motivo, e noi dobbiamo essere pronti a fare di più".

Vi sta sorprendendo Diawara? "Penso che si debba dare merito a Diawara. Sta lavorando davvero bene. Ha passato del tempo senza giocare e stava iniziando a provare un po' di frustrazione, ma ha continuato a lavorare duro nel modo giusto. Avrà la sua opportunità e si farà trovare pronto se continua a spingere così. Quindi il merito va tutto a Diawara. Credo che sia perfettamente in grado di coprire quel ruolo. Naturalmente dipende molto dall'avversario: una partita abbiamo giocato con Moreira da terzino e poi contro l'Inter abbiamo schierato Diawara. A volte si tratta della stessa posizione, ma con un giocatore diverso cambia completamente il mondo. Penso che sia pronto per farlo. Aveva già collezionato qualche minuto nella seconda divisione francese in quel ruolo e durante la sosta per le nazionali, nell'amichevole contro il Padova, lo abbiamo provato proprio da terzino sinistro, perché cerchiamo di sfruttare ogni singolo minuto per migliorare. Ha dato ottimi segnali: è forte, è veloce. Sapevamo quanto potessero essere pericolosi i cross, specialmente dalla catena di sinistra dell'Inter. Dimarco non ha giocato, ma l'idea tattica restava la stessa, e difendere sui traversoni con Koni e Pavlovic si è rivelata una buona intuizione. Hanno quasi segnato su un cross con Calhanoglu, ma credo stia facendo davvero benissimo. Ha ampi margini di crescita e chissà, magari domani partirà titolare".

Qual è il vostro punto di forza? "Ciò che dicevo sul fatto di vincere le partite, questa è la forza della squadra, la nostra identità: io metto sempre al primo posto il collettivo, non il singolo, anche se abbiamo ottime individualità. La punta del Ferencvaros è fortissima negli spazi: può giocare sia da esterno che da attaccante, e credo che contro di noi giocherà da punta. Nagy è un elemento importante perché capisce il gioco. Sa esattamente quando abbassarsi e quando invece restare alto, e questo genere di calciatori mi piace molto. A questo si aggiunge la qualità del terzino sinistro con il piede destro che sa accentrarsi: tutti questi piccoli dettagli definiscono un'identità che apprezzo molto in questa squadra, e dovremo farci trovare pronti a metabolizzare tutte queste informazioni per preparare e vincere la partita. Ripeto: abbiamo tre punti in questa competizione e domani dobbiamo assolutamente vincere".

Nel secondo tempo del derby si è visto un Milan autorevole... "Penso che sia un ottimo punto, ma per spiegare il secondo tempo bisogna partire dal primo, non si possono separare le due parti della gara. Credo sia importante capire che in una frazione abbiamo acquisito il vantaggio nel risultato, e poi abbiamo gestito la partita nella ripresa. Penso che stiamo migliorando nella lettura della gara: abbiamo dimostrato di poter essere una squadra molto forte perché abbiamo compreso ogni singolo momento del match, siamo stati davvero completi. Forse nel secondo tempo ci è mancato un pochino il coraggio di mettere uomini alle spalle dei centrocampisti dell'Inter per schiacciare ancora di più l'avversario verso la sua porta. Abbiamo fatto un buon possesso palla per gestirla, ed è stato positivo, ma dobbiamo fare il salto di qualità. Credo che la nostra ripresa contro la Lazio sia stata migliore, più intensa; era una partita diversa, lo capisco, ma possiamo ripartire da lì. Il punto è che si tratta pur sempre dell'Inter, e questo per me è il problema. Durante la settimana precedente alla partita con il Bologna, la gente, persino i tifosi, mi fermava dicendo: 'Buona fortuna per il derby'. Non lo capisco: il Bologna era la partita più importante per noi. Questo è il tipo di mentalità che non possiamo permetterci, è la mentalità da piccola squadra. Una piccola squadra si preoccupa solo dei grandi appuntamenti. No, no, no: ogni partita è un grande appuntamento. Quindi non lo so, la gara di domani dirà molto di più sulla mia squadra rispetto a quella con l'Inter. Se guardiamo alla storia recente, negli ultimi otto incroci contro l'Inter ne abbiamo vinti quattro, ma questo non mi diceva nulla. Il Ferencvaros, invece, mi dirà molto sulla mia squadra. Quindi aspettiamo domani: non mi interessa più quello che è stato con l'Inter. È stata una bella sensazione? Sì. È meglio che pareggiare o perdere? Certo, ma è il passato. E io sono ancora più arrabbiato per il Bologna che felice per l'Inter. Vediamo domani: dovremo essere davvero, davvero, davvero forti per vincere la partita".

Si emozionerà come Cardinale prima o poi? "Quando vinceremo lo Scudetto o un grande titolo, forse mi emozionerò; fino ad allora, è solo un altro giorno. Ma durante la partita ho avuto la sensazione che l'ambiente... beh, non mi aspettavo quell'atmosfera, e credo che neanche Cardinale se l'aspettasse. Ti rendi conto che si tratta di una scommessa importante e lui aveva appena fatto quell'intervista in cui sosteneva un allenatore di cui tutti dicevano che non vinceva ogni singola partita e via dicendo... Quindi alla fine della gara è stato un po' come dire: 'Forse so quello che sto facendo', non lo so. Quello che so è che l'atmosfera a San Siro era speciale e lui si è goduto quel momento. Ma l'emozione fa parte della passione: è americano, ma quando vivi qui per un po' finisci per diventare un po' italiano e portoghese, e questo è molto più di un gioco. Quindi capisco me stesso: non mi emozionerò finché non vinceremo, e quando vinceremo lo Scudetto, starò già pensando a quello successivo. Perciò credo che non mi vedrete mai così emozionato".

#2222. Middlesbrough man to remain sidelined until December

Middlesbrough will remain without the midfielder until the start of December. That means he is set to sit out of their upcoming games against Wrexham, Watford, Bristol City, Swansea City and Southampton.

Pukstas, 22, joined Boro in the summer on a long-term contract from Hadjuk Split running until June 2031. However, he has featured only once for the Championship promotion hopefuls.

In this latest update regarding his condition, his head coach Hellberg has said, as per a report by The Northern Echo: “He’s a month away, maybe, something like that. He’s a strong boy, he came from playing a lot and now he’s doing everything to come back stronger in every way he can. That’s how you try always to look at things, you can work on the things you can work at and try be stronger at that.”

Middlesbrough are sat top of the table after their first 13 fixtures ahead of the likes of Birmingham City, Stoke City, Swansea City and West Brom as they look to claw themselves into the Premier League. They face Wrexham away on Wednesday night.

Middlesbrough signed Pukstas in the last transfer window to bolster their midfield department. He gives them more competition and depth in the middle of the park.

At the age of 22, he has bags of potential and the capacity to grow and develop down the line. In the meantime, he faces a tough battle getting into Hellberg’s starting XI.

The USA youth international has some strong competition for minutes in his position. Boro have the likes of Aidan Morris, Sebastian Berhalter and Riley McGree, among others, at their disposal.

Pukstas started out at Sporting Kansas City before switching to Hadjuk Split as a teenager. He went on to become a key player for the Croatian outfit and scored 27 goals in 138 games before Middlesbrough lured him over to England for a new challenge.

Middlesbrough are having to be patient with Pukstas at the moment. He has struggled with injury since his switch and hasn’t played as much as he would have liked.

He is young though and still has plenty of time left ahead of him at Boro. He can still play a key role when he is back available and fit again as the matches come thick and fast over the December to January period.

Hellberg’s men will be full of confidence at the moment as they aim to keep their momentum going and build a gap at the summit. They beat Charlton Athletic 3-0 at home last time out and will be hoping for something similar against Wrexham next up.

#2220. Tributes paid after death of Tenerife striker following on-field collision

Tenerife player Jesus De Miguel has died after an on-field collision in a match on Monday, his club has announced.

The collision occurred as Andorra goalkeeper Jesus Owono raced from his goal to challenge De Miguel for the ball in stoppage time of a Spanish second-tier game.

The Canary Islands club said in a statement on Tuesday: “Racked with pain, with a lump in our throats and unable to believe that this is true, from CD Tenerife we communicate the tragic passing, this Tuesday, November 3, 2026, at 8:00 a.m., of Jesus de Miguel Alameda.

“There are no words of comfort; there is absolutely nothing that can alleviate this feeling overflowing with sadness.

Scotland star eyes dream Nou Camp return after childhood visit

Simo Valakari’s ‘two men short’ reveal as St Johnstone defy red card

Motherwell boss' ‘Sunday off’ threat revealed after ending seven-game wait

Late on Monday night Tenerife issued a statement confirming De Miguel had been admitted to hospital and was initially described as “stable despite the severity of his condition”.

An update in the early hours of Tuesday morning said his condition had “worsened neurologically”.

Owono was immediately sent off after he charged out of his goal to challenge De Miguel in the centre circle, his knee appearing to connect with the Tenerife player’s head.

Andorra and Tenerife players beckoned on medical staff immediately and appeared visibly upset by De Miguel’s condition.

The match was suspended after the incident.

#2219. Devastante in campionato, disastroso in Champions: ecco il Porto che affronterà il Napoli

Stasera alle 21 il Napoli di Massimiliano Allegri è chiamato ad affrontare il Porto in una sfida che mette di fronte alla compagine partenopea una compagine a due volti: quella dominante del campionato portoghese e quella fragile della Champions League. I Dragões di Francesco Farioli sono a punteggio pieno in Liga Portugal, ma nella League Phase della kermesse europea non hanno ancora raccolto un punto.

In patria il Porto non conosce ostacoli: dieci partite, dieci vittorie. Dopo il 4-0 all’Estoril di sabato 31 ottobre, la squadra è a 30 punti, con 25 gol segnati e soltanto 4 subiti. Tra i successi spicca il 3-1 al Benfica nella settima giornata, a cui si aggiungono i colpi in trasferta contro il Casa Pia (4-1) e l’Académico de Viseu (3-0).

Il quadro cambia completamente in Europa. Il Porto ha perso le prime tre gare: 0-2 in casa con il Manchester City, 3-2 in casa del Real Betis e 0-1 con il PSV Eindhoven. Il bilancio è di due gol fatti e sei subiti, con il 34º posto su 36 squadre.

Anche il Napoli arriva da un rendimento a due velocità. In Champions è 23º con 3 punti in tre gare, frutto di una vittoria e due sconfitte, con cinque gol fatti e sette subiti: il 4-3 al Bodo/Glimt è arrivato dopo i ko con l’Arsenal (0-1) e il Villarreal (3-1). In Serie A la situazione non è certamente migliore: gli azzurri sono 8º con 14 punti in dieci giornate (quattro vittorie, due pareggi e quattro sconfitte), con 17 gol segnati e 13 subiti, a 14 lunghezze dalla Lazio capolista.

#2218. Scott Parker’s first West Ham starting XI predicted as Cardiff City clash awaits – Tomas Soucek in

West Ham have acted quickly to replace the sacked Nuno Espirito Santo, naming Scott Parker as their new head coach on Wednesday morning. The former WHUFC captain jumps straight into the action too, as he will lead his new club in the clash with Cardiff City later tonight.

Parker will be backed by a first-team coaching staff including Steve Potts, Gerard Prenderville and Mark Noble, who have overseen preparations for the clash with the Bluebirds.

The new boss will need time to work out his strongest starting XI as he gets to grips with the squad at his disposal. However, his first lineup against Cardiff City could see some welcome reintroductions.

Hermansen; Veltman, Mavropanos, Kilman, Morato; Engels, Soucek; Bowen, Kante, Austbo; Piroe.

Parker has primarily played with a 4-2-3-1 formation over his managerial career to date. It is the system West Ham played in under Nuno too, so for the sake of continuity given the lack of time on the training ground under the new boss, it seems inevitable that they start in this setup against Cardiff City.

The new boss prefers his goalkeepers to be proficient in possession, as shown by James Trafford’s success in his Burnley team. As such, Mads Hermansen should keep his place ahead of Alphonse Areola despite recent questions over the Dane’s form.

Kyle Walker-Peters limped off in the defeat to West Brom, so Joel Veltman should start. Morato continues on the left flank, but in a big boost, Konstantinos Mavropanos may return in place of Airidas Golambeckis as he trained on Monday ahead of the game. If he is not fit though, the youngster will keep his spot.

In midfield, Tomas Soucek replacing Divine Mukasa seems a smart move to give Parker and WHUFC a bit more experience and physicality in midfield. He will partner Arne Engels, and Mohamadou Kante should retain his place in a more advanced roles.

Captain Jarrod Bowen is a shoo-in for a start on the right, and on the left, it’s a toss-up between Edvin Austbo and Manor Solomon. The latter is struggling for form though, so could be benched again.

Up top, Joel Piroe could be the proven Championship goalscorer Parker needs. He has Taty Castellanos and Pablo to pick from too.

It is a rarity to see a head coach appointed and lead their first game on the same day. However, Parker is wasting no time in getting to work with his new West Ham group.

He will lean on his coaching staff for the first game, before likely taking on a more leading role in team selection when WHUFC face Blackburn Rovers on Saturday. Parker will have had more time to assess his players and should have a better idea of who he wants in his preferred lineup.

Cardiff City will pose a tough test, as they look to dominate possession and control their games. The Bluebirds are unbeaten at home, winning their last three on their own patch against Birmingham City, Watford and Charlton Athletic.

Tonight’s game kicks off at 19:45 and will be broadcast live on Sky Sports+.

#2215. Tutti contro il Manchester City: la Premier chiede nuove indagini sulle finanze del club

Nuove nubi si addensano all'orizzonte per il Manchester City: diversi club di Premier League starebbero infatti spingendo per avviare una nuova inchiesta sulle finanze dei Citizens, concentrandosi in particolare sul periodo successivo al 2018. Questa mossa rischia di riaccendere le tensioni in tutto il calcio inglese, proprio mentre il club campione d'Inghilterra continua a contestare le conclusioni del procedimento finanziario già in corso.

Secondo quanto rivelato dal quotidiano The Independent, i dirigenti dei club rivali nutrono forti dubbi sul fatto che gli accordi di sponsorizzazione già finiti al centro del procedimento originale siano effettivamente cambiati dopo il 2018. Tuttavia, non c'è una linea comune: altre società si mostrano riluttanti all'idea di intraprendere un'altra lunga battaglia legale che potrebbe finire per danneggiare ulteriormente l'immagine e la reputazione della Premier League.

L'eventuale nuova indagine si troverebbe inoltre a fronteggiare notevoli ostacoli probatori, con diverse dirigenze preoccupate di non riuscire a raccogliere una documentazione sufficiente a supporto di nuove accuse, mentre altri club vedono la prospettiva di ulteriori azioni soprattutto come un'arma di pressione nella disputa in corso. Dal canto suo, il City respinge con forza ogni addebito e ribadisce la propria estraneità a qualsiasi illecito, ricordando che un'eventuale ulteriore inchiesta sarebbe comunque del tutto distinta dai procedimenti attuali, con sanzioni subordinate all'esito dei relativi processi legali.

#2214. Russell Martin ‘spoken highly of’ at Manchester United before Rangers stint

Former Rangers boss Russell Martin was “spoken highly of” by Manchester United technical director Jason Wilcox as the Old Trafford club weighed up potential replacements for Erik ten Hag in 2024.

Wilcox had previously worked with Martin at Southampton and regarded the former Scotland international as a manager worth monitoring for the future.

According to The Athletic, Martin was not considered a realistic candidate for the United job at that stage due to his relative lack of top-level experience, but Wilcox was impressed by his character, tactical understanding and commitment to possession-based football.

Pedro Caixinha back in Europe after joining 13th club of managerial career

Ex-Rangers star calls time on playing career after 17 years

Martin would later take charge of Rangers, but his spell at Ibrox proved ill-fated, lasting just 123 days. It proved another setback in Martin’s managerial career after his time with Southampton had ended in relegation from the Premier League.

But the revelation of Wilcox’s admiration provides an intriguing insight into how highly Martin was regarded before his eventual move to Rangers.

Wilcox had appointed him at Southampton in 2023 and backed him through a difficult start before the club embarked on a club-record 25-match unbeaten run and secured promotion to the Premier League through the play-offs.

#2213. City fire blanks in shoot-out as Maresca’s opening game ends in defeat by Inter

Manchester City lost the Asahi Super Dry Trophy 3-1 on a penalty shoot-out against Inter Milan.

Enzo Maresca took charge of the Premier  League runners-up for the first time since his arrival as Pep Guardiola’s replacement, though he was without many of his stars who had yet to return from World Cup duty.

One of the players missing was Elliot Anderson, the £116m signing from Nottingham Forest, though Jeremy Monga, 16, was an unused substitute after being brought in from Leicester City in the summer transfer window.

City took the lead on 14 minutes through Divin Mubamba as he tapped in an Antoine Semenyo cross, but Inter’s experienced defender Benjamin Pavard levelled just six minutes later when City failed to clear a corner.

The Premier League side dominated possession in the second half after an even first 45 minutes but could not find a way through. Phil Foden, the captain, was again underwhelming after a difficult year last season, but with the season still to come he had plenty of time to show his best form once more after signing a new contract at the Etihad.

The game went to penalties after full-time with no extra time played, and only Claudio Echeverri held his nerve for City as Inter Milan scored three of theirs, Matteo Lavelli netting the winning spot-kick.

Both teams learnt little from the match as Inter made 11 changes and City eight, though Maresca will have been impressed by Ryan McAidoo’s performance as a second-half substitute, as he regularly threatened from the right wing. The 18-year-old forward will surely be in demand from other clubs looking to loan him, and City may yet be tempted to keep him around for the coming season.

Manchester City Donnarumma; Lewis, Khusanov, Gvardiol (Reis, 46), Mfuni (Alleyne, 46); Kovacic (N González, 46), Reijnders (Ait-Nouri, 46); Savinho (Braithwaite, 78), Foden (Echeverri, 68), Semenyo (Sangare, 68); Mubama (McAidoo, 46).Substitutes not used Bettinelli, Wint, Chabot, Monga, Mukasa, F. Samba, Heskey, Henderson-Hall, Parker.Booked Khusanov (83).Goal Mubama (14).Inter Milan Martinez (Provedel, 61); Augusto (Marello, 69), Bisseck (Maye, 78), Pavard (Bovio, 69); Dimarco (Bastoni, 46), Mkhitaryan (Zielinski, 46), Stankovic (Topalovic, 60), Barella (Frattesi, 46), Diouf (Henrique, 46); Iddrissou (Mosconi, 46), Esposito (Lavelli, 67).Substitutes not used Di Gennaro, Farronato, Sucic, Bonny, Calhanoglu.Booked Stankovic (55).Goal Pavard (20).

Lavelli blasts his shot down the middle, and Inter have won the Asahi Trophy!

The teenager sizes things up, and sends Donnarumma the other way.

A stuttering run, and Provedel beats it away.

Frattesi misses! Donnarumma stretches out and flings up his left arm for a great save.

Khusanov misses, firmly striking against the post.

Donnarumma dives to the right, the shot in the opposite direction.

Rayan Ait-Nouri misses! Spooned over the bar.

We’re onto the penalty shootout. The pressure builds for the Asahi Trophy.

Echeverri is fouled in midfield, he takes it quickly, but the move breaks down and Inter get back into position again. The end nears.

Three more minutes of this have been indicated.

Gonzalez finds McAidoo, and City look for room on the right. Inter sit back and stay compact.

The game has slowed to a near-halt. It seems everyone is resigned to penalties.

Ait-Nouri finds McAidoo’s run to the back post with a fabulous low cross, but the winger’s return ball is cut out by Provedel.

If McAidoo does not stay on at City for the season ahead, you’d expect plenty of sides to be looking to bring him in on loan.

Ait-Nouri is offside as he takes the ball on the left wing, and Inter have it back briefly.

McAidoo yet again gets forward and almost forces a cross past Provedel. The ball comes back to Sangare, but his effort is blocked. City are getting closer.

Khusanov is booked for a foul in midfield, and then is on hand to block a shot on the line as Inter fail to convert.

McAidoo, yet again. A shot to the far post, yet again. A miss, yet again. He looks dangerous though.

McAidoo repeats the trick, but this time he keeps his shot low and hits the bottom of the far post. The best moment of the half so far.

However, with the scores still level, it’s only 10 minutes from a penalty shootout.

McAidoo scoots into the box from the right and curls a shot wide of the far post.

Enzo makes another change 🔄 pic.twitter.com/afvwMFYlB9

Savinho slices a shot wildly high and wide. Changes are coming.

Lewis has the ball in the box after quick feet from Savinho with the assist, and he prods the ball at Provedel.

McAidoo is released down the inside left, he clears his marker and aims for Semenyo, but Bisseck clears for a corner.

Pavard goes down after he is caught late from Ait-Nouri, but he’s fine to continue.

More subs now  Topalovic replaces Stankovic. Provedel replaces Martinez in goal.

Savinho might be the most dangerous player for City today, a sentence that has rarely been true in the last couple of years. McAidoo whips in a cross, which Henrique clears under no pressure.

Foden commits his own foul in midfield, this time on Mkhitaryan. There are a few minutes left before half-time, at which point we may see a few changes from both sides given the early stage of pre-season.

Foden is tugged down in midfield, with the City man still failing to show much of his talent in the new season.

Mkhitaryan continues to find space in pockets on the left. In general, Inter are finding it very easy to trundle to the edge of the City box.

Do you think the players are coping without a hydration break?

City have some pressure and Kovacic hits a group of defenders with a volley from outside the box. It’s meek stuff from Maresca’s men so far but obviously, too early to draw much from it.

City are looking to build from the back through the middle, but they are quickly crowded out. Inter come forward once more.

Diouf forces a corner on the right wing as Donnarumma clears a cross. It’s taken short, Inter switch the ball left, but Mkhitaryan overhits a pass to the byline.

Mkhitaryan receives the ball on the left, inside the box, in another dangerous position. Lewis had drifted  too far inside, but the danger passes when the forward is flagged offside.

Inter are keeping the ball calmly at the back, finding spaces between the pressing City attackers.

They break through and Donnarumma beats away a low shot from Stankovic.

Divin Mubamba gets the opener! Semenyo beats his right-bacck and crosses to the six-yard box for Mubamba to tap in.

Dimarco volleys wide but he too was offside, and then Martinez saves from Reijnders at the other end. It’s a free-flowing match so far.

Stankovic goes close with an early header after Inter win their first corner of the match. It’s an open game so far.

City win two early corners, but they are both cleared. A bright start for the Premier League side. Esposito then goes close at the other end, but he was offside anyway.

Welcome to Telegraph Sport’s live coverage of the pre-season friendly between Manchester City and Inter Milan.

The two sides meet  at Kai Tak Sports Park, Hong  Kong as their pre-season work kicks up a gear ahead of the new campaign.

City are still getting used to life without Pep Guardiola, the coach who left after a decade of high spending and high performance.

In his place is Enzo Maresca, who is not shy with the chequebook himself.

Ayyoub Bouaddi, the outstanding 18-year-old Moroccan international, should soon arrive from Lille when a fee is agreed, but Elliot Anderson and Jeremy Monga have already been signed.

City were runners-up last season, so Maresca is under pressure not just to keep things going without Guardiola, but to get the team back to the top of English football. That looks to be a tough prospect with Arsenal likely to sign Bruno Guimaraes from Newcastle in the coming days.

Inter, meanwhile, have swooped to pick up John Stones on a free transfer after his contract ended at the Etihad Stadium, and he is joined by Manuel Akanji, another former City centre-back whose loan turned permanent in the summer.

Inter won Serie A last season under head coach Cristian Chivu, and they are still one of the best sides in Europe.

While this friendly is likely to be played at a reduced pace, and will be disrupted by rustiness and substitutes, we could still learn a lot about both sides going into the new campaign, and there may be the odd surprise thrown up by a young player looking to stake a claim ahead of his senior colleagues this year.

#2212. Jermain Defoe in line for coaching role with 46-year-old set to become Bromley boss

Bromley parted ways with Andy Woodman last month, in a controversial dismissal after five successful years in charge. Woodman had taken the side from the National League to League One, however, they have struggled this season and are bottom of the third tier table.

Byron Webster has been in charge on an interim basis. Now though, reporter Jason Burt states that Karl Robinson is set to join as the Ravens’ new manager.

Robinson has been without a job since June, following his departure from Salford City. He led the side to the League Two play-off final last season, losing out on promotion to Notts County.

Robinson, 46, is set to bring an assistant of his own with him to Hayes Lane, as Burt adds Jermain Defoe is poised to join alongside the new boss. He will serve as no.2 to the experienced manager following a maiden managerial stint of his own at Woking.

At the time of his first managerial appointment, Robinson was aged just 29 with MK Dons – the youngest boss in the EFL at the time. He spent six years with the Dons and has since managed Salford City, Charlton Athletic and Oxford United.

At each of his sides, aside from Charlton Athletic, Robinson has managed over 130 games. He averaged over 1.5 points per game at all of Salford, Oxford and MK, with his Addicks stint being the only exception again at 1.36 PPG.

Robinson often operates with a 3-4-1-2, but his vast experience has seen him switch systems and utilise four-man defences. He likes his sides to have high possession, with wide overloads, aggressive pressing and fluid midfield rotations.

A past shift to a 5-2-1-2 could be repeated at Bromley to provide them with more defensive solidity in their bid to secure League One survival.

In his time as a manager, Robinson has gained most of his experience in League One. He has won 796 points in the division, including 222 wins (Transfermarkt).

Defoe’s experience is more limited, but he is a budding coach determined to forge his way in the dugout after a short spell in charge of Woking. The former England striker has had roles at Tottenham Hotspur and Rangers alongside his stint with the Cardinals, and his experience as a top player could mean he has valuable nuggets of advice to offer to the players.

Bromley have mainly played in a 4-1-4-1 system this season, and it was regularly used last term alongside a 3-4-2-1. They may have to adjust to new demands under Robinson.

Bromley do not have a league fixture until November 21st now, but will hope Robinson can make an impression in cup matches against Rotherham United and MK Dons as he gets to work at Hayes Lane.

Robinson has the experience and tactical nous to bring success at Bromley, but time will tell whether the squad is truly strong enough to achieve such a feat after their quick ascent to League One.

#2211. Milan, Amorim: "Prima del Bologna mi chiedevano del derby. Mentalità da piccola"

“L’Inter fa parte del passato, dobbiamo difendere bene anche domani”. Ruben Amorim, alla vigilia della sfida tra il suo Milan e il Ferencvaros, parla così del derby vinto nel weekend, soffermandosi anche sul secondo tempo: “Non possiamo scindere quella prestazione da quella del primo, altrimenti non la spieghiamo per bene. Bisogna capire che nel primo tempo siamo andati in vantaggio per quanto riguarda il risultato, e poi è stato fondamentale il modo di difendere la partita nella seconda frazione.

Siamo migliorati nella comprensione del gioco, abbiamo dimostrato di poter diventare una bella squadra perché siamo stati bravi in tutti i reparti. Forse ci è mancato mettere qualche giocatore dietro le linee dell’Inter, abbiamo avuto tanti giocatori in grado di fare un buon possesso palla. Il secondo tempo con la Lazio è stato altrettanto intenso.

Il problema è che era con l’Inter… In settimana abbiamo giocato con il Bologna e tutti i tifosi mi dicevano in bocca al lupo per il derby: non lo capisco, perché il Bologna in quel momento era la cosa più importante. È una mentalità da piccola squadra, che non possiamo permetterci di avere. Io domani capirò di più la mia squadra rispetto alla partita con l’Inter. Abbiamo vissuto una bella sensazione, ma sono ancora più arrabbiato per la sconfitta con il Bologna che per la vittoria con l'Inter”.

#2210. Martin O'Neill and Celtic chiefs given ‘hard but fair’ grilling at recent meeting

Celtic manager Martin O’Neill and senior club figures faced more than two hours of “hard but fair” questioning from supporters at a packed meeting in Greenock.

Around 120 fans attended the Greenock Celtic Supporters’ Club on Monday night, with recruitment, transfer policy, communication and the club’s ambitions and strategy among the issues raised.

Per Celtic's statement on what transpired, O’Neill was joined by interim chairman Brian Wilson, chief executive Michael Nicholson, chief financial officer Chris McKay and other club officials for the two-and-a-half-hour question-and-answer session.

Wilson admitted the Celtic hierarchy had been prepared for tough questioning.

He said: “We didn’t expect an easy ride and didn’t get one, but the meeting was conducted in a constructive and mutually respectful way and the messages delivered by supporters will be taken on board and learned from.”

Celtic Fans Collective demand Dermot Desmond attend AGM in person and face scrutiny

Celtic Europa League rivals make shock decision to sack history-making boss

Furious Besiktas star turns on team-mates ahead of crunch Celtic showdown

Supporters from Greenock, Port Glasgow, Gourock, Johnny Doyle, Port Glasgow Hibs and Largs clubs were among those represented.

Nicholson also welcomed the opportunity to hear directly from fans and insisted everyone involved shared the same desire to see Celtic succeed.

He said: “Everyone in the room wants the best for Celtic and that was evident.

“We are grateful for supporters’ input and look forward to continuing to meet with supporters as we work on improving communication and engagement in the weeks and months ahead.”

Celtic say further details on the club’s new Celtic Connect engagement initiative and future fans’ forums will be announced soon.

The Greenock gathering followed recent meetings with the Affiliation of Registered CSCs in Glasgow and the Association of Irish Celtic Supporters' Clubs in Cork.

#2209. Three goals conceded: Ex-Sheffield Wednesday man endures a tough night on UEFA Champions League debut

Eyebrows will have been raised in both Sheffield and Rome when Devis Vasquez was picked to start for AS Roma in their UEFA Champions League clash against Manchester United on Tuesday night. The ex-Sheffield Wednesday loan man has served as backup ‘keeper in Mile Svilar’s absence, but came into the first XI at Old Trafford.

All was going well for former SWFC loan man Vasquez and Roma as they went 2-0 up within 17 minutes. However, the Colombian shot-stopper would concede three second-half goals as United fought back to win 3-2.

Vasquez made two saves but finished with an xG prevented of -0.50. having conceded three times from an xG of 2.50 (Fotmob). He was nearly a hero as he saved a penalty from Bruno Fernandes in the second half, but Roma’s Bryan Cristante was cruelly deemed to have encroached and the Manchester United man fired home the retake.

Vasquez was a 26-year-old goalkeeper on the books of AC Milan when he joined Sheffield Wednesday on loan in 2023. He came in and was the Owls’ starting no.1 under Xisco Munoz, but was dropped from the side after the Spaniard’s sacking and would never play for the club again.

The Long-serving Cameron Dawson stepped back into the starting role, before James Beadle joined in January. Vasquez was then recalled by Milan and promptly loaned out to Ascoli. Almost his entire time with I Rossoneri was spent out on temporary deals, and when he was released in 2025, Roma snapped him up.

Vasquez has served as cover while with Rome and did so in a half-season loan at Besiktas in 2025/26 too. He played once for the Turkish giants, keeping a clean sheet in a 0-0 draw with Fatih Karamguruk back in April.

Barring his loans to SWFC and second-tier Italian sides Ascoli and Empoli, Vasquez has mainly served as a cover option for all of his clubs. The now 28-year-old has the pride of making his UEFA Champions League debut though, despite the result.

Vasquez is looked back on as a fairly minor part of the Sheffield Wednesday side that endured dismal fortunes under Xisco Munoz. He didn’t give a great account of himself with a save percentage of only 59% while at Hillsborough (Fotmob), but the Owls had far bigger problems than their loan goalkeeper at the time as they went winless in their first 10 Championship games that season.

After the Colombian, the Owls had far better fortunes in the goalkeeping department. He was succeeded by loan hit Beadle in January, and the Brighton & Hove Albion prospect would return for the 2024/25 campaign.

The emergence of Pierce Charles would gather pace too, as he cemented himself as one of the UK’s brightest goalkeeping prospects despite shoulder injuries.

Now, as Vasquez earns opportunities with Roma, SWFC have Joe Lumley and Ashley Maynard-Brewer battling for the starting berth. The new ‘keepers will hope to play key roles under new boss Dave Challinor as the club rebuild after administration and relegation.

#2208. Damiani, Silipo e Brunori, i tre dell'Ascoli pronti a sfidare il loro passato rosanero

Venerdì sera ad Ascoli si aprirà l’undicesima giornata di Serie B con una sfida che vedrà i padroni di casa affrontare un Palermo che è capolista del campionato e ancora imbattuto dopo dieci giornate. Una sfida che per tre giocatori del club marchigiano, attualmente terzo con sette punti di ritardo dai rosanero, avrà un sapore speciale visto il loro passato nel club siciliano con cui hanno conquistato la promozione in Serie B nella stagione 2021/22.

I primi due ex sono il centrocampista Samuele Damiani e l’esterno offensivo Andrea Silipo: il primo arrivò nel gennaio del 2022 dall’Empoli diventando subito un tassello importante nello scacchiere di Silvio Baldini, che a dicembre aveva sostituiti Giacomo Filippi, con cui collezionò 21 presenze fra stagione regolare e play off. Anche il classe 2001 era in quel Palermo, ma da più tempo. Silipo infatti era arrivato due anni prima, nell’anno della ripartenza dalla Serie D contribuendo con due gol alla promozione. Due le reti anche nella stagione vincente in Serie C quando scese in campo in 25 occasioni. Per entrambi l’addio arrivò nella stagione successiva.

All’inizio di quella stagione in Serie C il colpo di mercato fu però Matteo Brunori, reduce da alcune stagioni opache con Pescara, Juventus Next Gen e Virtus Entella. Il suo inizio a Palermo fu di quelli da ricordare: 29 reti in 44 presenze che lo fecero diventare immediatamente idolo della piazza rosanero dove è rimasto fino alla metà della passata stagione indossando a lungo anche la fascia da capitano. E continuando a segnare gol pesanti – 76 in totale in 175 presenze – pur senza riuscire a coronare il sogno del salto in Serie A. Scalato nelle gerarchie alle spalle di Pohjanpalo e finito fuori dai radar di Inzaghi nella passata stagione l’ex capitano dopo sei mesi alla Sampdoria è ripartito da Ascoli dove finora ha segnato solo un gol in 7 presenze. E chissà se contro la sua ex squadra non possa trovare nuovamente la gioia della rete.

#2207. Three goals from 1.27 xG: Sydie Peck defies the numbers to break seven-year Sheffield United duck

Sheffield United continued their fine form on Tuesday night as they defeated Preston North End 3-2 away from home. SUFC are now four games without defeat, and they’ve won four of their last six Championship matches.

It was a strong team performance from the Blades, but the man-of-the-match display from hat-trick hero Sydie Peck can not be overlooked. The 22-year-old midfielder scored three in the first half, becoming the first United player to score a competitive first-team hat-trick since Billy Sharp against Aston Villa in February 2019.

Peck did so from an expected goals (xG) of just 1.27 too. First, his cross bounced all the way through and beyond Daniel Iversen (0.02 xG) before he kept the Preston North End ‘keeper at bay and floated beyond a despairing defence for his second (0.21 xG). Finally, the Blades star slid in at the back post to convert from Romelle Donovan’s cross (0.81 xG) to seal his hat-trick.

Peck registered a total of 1.27 xG across his six shots – the most by anyone in the game. His attacking threat was emphasised by the fact his six touches in the opposition box was more than any other player too.

The Sheffield United man saw to his usual duties. He created two chances in total and completed 52 passes, also winning six out of seven aerial duels – a tally bettered by only Mark McGuinness in the SUFC side (Fotmob).

It was the complete midfield performance from Peck, who has grown in influence this season. His importance creatively is displayed by 21 chances created and 76 line-breaking passes, and 779 touches shows how regularly he is the man to get on the ball when the Blades have possession.

Peck has made 54 defensive contributions too though, winning 52 duels in total. This shows his willingness to get stuck in and do the dirty work, while 50 recoveries highlights his work rate as well (Fotmob).

Now on four goals this season, if Peck can start to score on a more consistent basis, he will really be a complete midfielder for Chris Wilder.

Peck has been with Sheffield United for over five years now, joining the academy after his exit from Arsenal. He broke into the team in the 2024/25 campaign and would grow in the 2025/26 season with five goals and five assists in 41 games across all competitions.

The London-born midfielder drew interest from West Ham in the summer, but he expressed a desire to pay back all those who have shown faith in him at Bramall Lane – including manager Wilder.

Peck is happy with SUFC and his continued improvements this season show his development isn’t being impacted by sticking around either. However, if he continues in his current form, interest is bound to grow, and exit opportunities will become more tempting.

Sheffield United are keen to renew Peck’s contract as his current deal runs out in 2028. It would be wise to strike an agreement sooner rather than later with clubs sure to be alerted by his impressive displays of late.

#2206. Exciting young talent JJ Gabriel makes debut as Man Utd beat Atletico Madrid

JJ Gabriel showed glimpses of his potential as he made his Manchester United debut in their 2-1 win over Atletico Madrid in Stockholm.

The 15-year-old may have been introduced with only eight minutes remaining, but, given how highly rated he is, it was a significant move by Michael Carrick to give him game time in the senior team.

There were hints of why Gabriel is so well regarded during those eight minutes, as he found space in the centre of the pitch and linked well with Leny Yoro. But he was also on the receiving end of some physical challenges – something he will have to grow accustomed to the more he plays at senior level.

Yoro, who himself made his senior debut as a 16-year-old for Lille, was impressed by Gabriel and said: “He’s a really good player. He is still really young and still has a lot to learn and a lot to improve on but he’s really humble and still working, so I’m happy for him to get his first minutes. I hope, for him, it’s going to continue like that.”

United fought back after conceding an early goal against Atletico to secure their second win of pre-season.

They fell behind in the sixth minute when Arnau Ortiz’s cross into the box evaded everyone, including United keeper Tom Heaton before hitting the back of the net.

United got the equaliser their performance deserved when the impressive Shea Lacey showed his skill in the box and was fouled. From the resulting penalty, Bryan Mbeumo sent the goalkeeper the wrong way from the spot.

In the 72nd minute, Mbeumo got his second of the afternoon after he bundled the ball home after the United press forced Atletico into a mistake.

The Spanish side hit the post twice in the closing stages but United held on to win.

“We had a clear plan before the game, everyone stuck to it and made the game enjoyable,” Mbeumo said. “We work really hard during training for these games, the main goal is to be ready for the season starting. I have done great things on the right but also as a striker.

“I think I am more experienced on the wing but I enjoy playing as a striker. For an offensive player, it is always good to score for the team.”

Martínez 61), Ruggeri (Romeo 61), Koke (Hjulmand 46), Obed Vargas (Mendoza 46), Castillo (Iker Luque 61), Arnau Ortiz (Sergio Esteban 61), Carlos Martín (Lemar 61), Lookman (Solà 61)Goals: Arnau Ortiz (5)

And it is. All over in Stockholm as United come back from behind to win. A really good performance by Michael Carrick’s side.

Iker Luque shoots from distance. It looks good but flies over the bar. And that should be the final effort of the match...

Mendoza and Hjulmand both hit the post in quick succession. Heaton was beaten on both occasions. United were a bit fortunate there.

Now that they are behind, Atletico are starting to have a bit more possession and play on the front foot.

A slow second half comes alive as United take the lead. A slack pass in defence by Atletico is pounced upon by Fletcher. He runs to the byline, cuts the ball back to the unmarked Mbeumo, who taps in.

OFF: Shaw, Dorgu, Lacey, MaguireON: Armer, Amass, Zirkzee, Williams

Big save from Heaton to deny Atletico at the near post after Yoro was beaten by a lovely pass from Lemar.

The energy and intensity of the first half has largely disappeared in this half. Neither keeper has been worked.

OFF: Domínguez, Hancko, Ruggeri, Arnau, Castillo, Carlos Martín, Lookman.ON: Boñar, Solà, D. Martínez, Lemar, Romeo, Iker Luque, Sergio Esteban.

Another player, who has been tidy for United is Santos in midfield. He’s controlled the middle of the park, been safe in possession but also willing to fire a pass into the forwards.

Seven changes coming for Atletico. Typical pre-season move.

Mbeumo takes responsibility, waits for the keeper to dive and strokes the ball into the bottom left corner.

Dancing feet from Lacey in the box and Castillo brings him down. The referee rightly points to the spot.

Heaven is booked for a late tackle after Atletico threatened a counter-attack.

Amad can be very pleased after his first minutes of pre-season. He was very lively.

OFF: Oblak, Le Normand, Koke, Obed VargasON: Esquivel, Giménez, Mendoza, Hjulmand

J. Fletcher coming for United in place of Amad.

Atletico make three changes. I’ll get them to you shortly!

No time added on, so that is the end of the half. An intriguing 45 mins. United will feel they don’t deserve to be losing.

United fail to clear the ball and it falls to Arnau Ortiz, who forces a good save from Heaton. That would have been harsh on United.

Lookman has been very quiet for Atletico. Yoro has marked him out of the game but in truth, Atletico have given him nothing to work with.

Apart from the move that led to Atletico’s goal, they have barely been in United’s half. They are struggling to beat United’s press and keep the ball. United are losing but they are working very hard and playing well.

Great pressing by United leads to Amad winning the ball back. Yoro finds Lacey, who spins and goes down the right. He whips in a cross and Mbeumo rises to attack it but heads wide. Probably should have done better.

It is probably an easy comparison but Lacey has a bit of Phil Foden about him with his movement and touch. He looks promising.

Carlos Martín goes down after a coming together with Heaven. The United defender got his arm across and made minimal contact with Martín’s face but the referee falls for the play-acting and calls a foul.

An aggressive press from United as they look to deny time to Atletico. They are pushing for that equaliser.

Amad, Mount and Mbeumo all want it. Amad takes it and his low strike is deflected and looks certain to beat Oblak but the keeper reacts quickly to make the stop.

Santos punches a pass through the lines, Mbeumo combines with Mount and the attacker is brought to the ground on the edge of the box...

Nearly a quick reply by United. Amad sets the ball for Mount to cross into the box. The midfielder’s ball goes to the far post, where Shaw meets it with a thumping volley but Oblak stands his ground and palms the ball over the bar.

From the resulting corner, Yoro should do better with his header but his effort goes wide.

Early goal for Atletico. They take a short corner, Arnau Ortiz whips in a dangerous ball that beats everyone and drops in at the far post. Heaton never moved.

United dominating possession in the opening stages with Atletico happy to sit off and let the Premier League side have it. Even in pre-season, Diego Simeone has his side set up well to defend.

The visit to the Strawberry Arena means United are back at the stadium where they won the 2017 Europa League.

📸 Wayne Rooney, 2017 🏆#UEL | @ManUtd pic.twitter.com/HxZVn1mAEQ

Gianni Infantino is facing an ultimatum from Uefa: resign or face an emergency no-confidence vote.

It is understood all 55 of Uefa’s member nations would opt to oust Infantino in a vote of no-confidence if he refuses to step down. Uefa can trigger such a vote with just 43 member nations.

European football’s governing body announced a loss of confidence on Saturday morning and has demanded change after Infantino was forced to scrap his £15bn plan to sell a stake in the World Cup.

Uefa’s statement followed widespread opposition and a revolt within Fifa’s ranks that staff are calling “kill the monster”.

The Football Association backed Uefa’s stance, saying: “We fully support Uefa’s position. It is time for a full and robust review of Fifa’s leadership and governance to ensure that the global game is run transparently, for the benefit of all 211 member nations and with the long-term stewardship of football at its heart.”

Atletico: Oblak, Domínguez, Le Normand, Hancko, Ruggeri, Koke, Obed Vargas, Castillo, Arnau Ortiz, Carlos Martín, Lookman

United: Heaton; Yoro, Maguire (c), Heaven, Shaw; Santos, Mount; Amad, Lacey, Dorgu; Mbeumo.Substitutes: Bayindir, Mee, Vitek, Amass, Armer, Kamason, J. Fletcher, T. Fletcher, Thwaites, Gabriel, Williams, Zirkzee.

Good afternoon and welcome to pre-season coverage of Manchester United against Atletico Madrid.

Michael Carrick’s squad continue their preparations for the new season with a trip to the Swedish capital, Stockholm, where they face Diego Simeone’s La Liga side.

Last week, United cruised to a 5-0 victory over Rosenborg but today will be their first real test. They are slowly starting to get players back but the likes of captain Bruno Fernandes and Youri Tielemans will not be involved.

“I think we’re in a good place. I think there’s four weeks to go to the start and we’re gradually getting some boys back from the World Cup as we progress,” Carrick said.

“But I think a little bit of patience and time and trying to keep ahead and as I said, keeping everyone fit but moving forward is a really good direction to go in. And as it stands right now, I think we’re in a pretty good place. So, the boys will get better as we go.”

One player who will be looking to impress is Mason Mount. He has had an injury-hit spell at Old Trafford but is fit and ready to go for the season. He is also growing into a leadership role at the club.

He told BBC Radio Manchester: “You have different types of leaders, you have ones that are very vocal. I always want to see myself as one that leads by example and never stops working on the pitch.

“I’ve been captain previously years ago. I love the role especially with a lot of younger players on the pitch being able to speak to them and make them feel comfortable in the game and off the pitch as well. It’s a role that I really like and loved having it [the captain’s armband] in the second half.”

#2205. SPFL reveals Rangers vs Hibs final date, time, ticket split and prices

Rangers and Hibernian have been handed a 50/50 split of Hampden for next month’s Premier Sports Cup final.

The sides will meet at the national stadium on Sunday, December 13, with the showpiece scheduled for a 3pm kick-off and broadcast live on Premier Sports.

Confirmed match arrangements and ticket information for next month's 2026/27 Premier Sports Cup final 🏆 https://t.co/Iaq1uil4L4

The SPFL has confirmed the ticketing arrangements following discussions with both clubs and the relevant authorities.

Hibernian supporters will be housed across the South, East and North Stands, while Rangers fans will be located across the South, West and North Stands.

Ticket prices will be the same for both sets of supporters.

The majority of adult tickets will cost £42, with adult seats in the North and South Stands priced at £49.

Concessionary tickets will also be available across the stadium, priced at £27 or £30 depending on the section.

Rangers secured their place in the final by defeating Aberdeen last Saturday, with Ryan Naderi scoring a late winner in the semi-final.

Hibernian booked their Hampden return a day later with a 2-1 victory over Edinburgh rivals Hearts.

All tickets will be issued digitally through the Barclays Hampden app, with both clubs set to announce their respective sales information through their own channels.

It will be only the second time Rangers and Hibs have met in the final of the competition.

Their previous meeting came in the 1993/94 final at Celtic Park, when Rangers won 2-1.

#2203. How much West Ham paid to sack Nuno Espirito Santo after missing the chance to do it for free

West Ham made the decision to sack Nuno Espirito Santo on Monday, after a 3-1 home defeat to West Brom. WHUFC have acted quickly to hire Scott Parker as their new boss, but they had to pay a sizeable compensation fee to part ways with Nuno.

The Athletic states that the Hammers paid around £2m to relieve the Portuguese boss of his duties. This is after having the option to do so for nothing after their relegation from the Premier League was confirmed in May.

New manager Parker had the support of board members as early as May, before opting to stick by Nuno. Mark Noble was among the 46-year-old’s strongest backers but Dutch coach John Heitinga was also considered as a potential replacement.

As soon as the decision was made to stick by Nuno in the summer, the pressure was on for the West Ham boss. He failed to keep them in the Premier League, but there was hope he could get them back there having led Wolves to Championship promotion in impressive fashion in 2017/18.

There were encouraging signs, as the Hammers rose as high as top of the table during a run of 10 Championship games unbeaten. They scored for fun too, scoring 30 times in the first 11 matches, including big wins over Wrexham, Lincoln City (both 6-0), Derby County (3-0) and Wolves (4-2).

However, frustrations over the style of football continued with cautious play in possession persisting despite WHUFC’s star power in attack. Defensive concerns persisted too, and when the warning signs led to defeats against Southampton and west Ham, the crowd had turned on Nuno.

United are ultimately made to pay for sticking by Nuno in the summer – £2m to be exact. The appointment of Parker for nothing limits the expense of this managerial change, but when the Portuguese boss could have gone in the summer for nothing, it has proven to be a costly decision by the club.

West Ham’s appointment of Parker has led to a mixed response. Many are pleased to see a former Hammers star and three-time Championship promotion-winning manager join the club, but there are some reservations over his style of play.

Like Nuno, Parker’s tactics in recent jobs have been built on a solid defensive foundation, showing a willingness to let the opposition have the ball, and when his sides do have it, playing conservatively.

However, Parker has adapted his tactics over time. While in charge of Fulham, his side had the second-highest average possession in the Championship with 60.8% (Fotmob), and they went on to win the league. They also recorded the highest xG (90.4 – 20 more than any other team), most big chances created (136) and most touches in the opposition box (1,352).

It will be intriguing to see if Parker reverts to this, or sticks by the defence-first tactics that saw him win promotion with Burnley after conceding only 16 goals in 46 matches.

WHUFC supporters want promotion at any cost, but the criticisms of Nuno’s style of play suggest they would rather brings more forward-thinking and controlling football.

#2202. Rangers youth prospect reveals personal ‘privilege’ of working with boyhood hero

Rangers youngster Rydnn McGuire has opened up on the “privilege” of working alongside his former goalkeeping hero Allan McGregor at Ibrox.

McGregor returned to Rangers as a coach and is now helping develop the next generation of goalkeepers, including McGuire, who has spent time around the first-team set-up this season.

🗣️ "It's a chance for everyone to go and showcase their skills to a lot of people." Rydnn McGuire spoke to @RangersTV ahead of tomorrow evening's #UYL second leg clash against Dynamo Kyiv at Forthbank Stadium. 🎟️ https://t.co/dzAtggjPPN https://t.co/kA5EgInsvc

— Rangers Academy (@RFC_Youth) November 3, 2026

Speaking to Rangers club media ahead of Wednesday’s UEFA Youth League second leg against Dynamo Kyiv, McGuire revealed he grew up watching the former Scotland international.

He said: “Very good. It’s a privilege to come and work with him every day.

“He was probably my generation of Rangers goalie growing up, so I watched him from a young age, and he’s been really good to work with.”

McGuire has combined his involvement around the senior squad with appearances in the KDM Evolution Trophy and Youth League this season.

The young goalkeeper believes that mixture has been important for his development rather than simply training without getting competitive minutes.

He said: “I think it’s critical in what I need just now.

“To come down and play these games, and they’re high-level games, they are challenging games that I’m coming down and playing, so it’s getting experience from everything.”

McGuire was part of the Rangers youth side whose success last season earned them the chance to compete in Europe and was determined not to miss out after making the step up to the first-team environment.

He said: “It was the first thing I said to Greegsie when I went round. I don’t want all the hard work I did last year to go to waste and not getting to get to play in it, so I made sure my stance was that I wanted to play in these games.

“They’ve been really good, and they have let me play in these games, so a massive thanks to them for letting me do that.”

Russell Martin ‘spoken highly of’ at Manchester United before Rangers stint

Pedro Caixinha back in Europe after joining 13th club of managerial career

Unseen moment Rangers star warned 'job's not done' by team-mate after semi-final win

Attention now turns to Wednesday’s return against Dynamo Kyiv, with Rangers still in the tie due to the 3-2 scoreline, following two second-half goals in the first leg.

McGuire admits the Light Blues will have to produce an almost flawless performance if they are to progress.

He said: “The information we’re getting from Stevie and the staff, we believe we can go and pull it off. We probably need to be as close to perfect as we can on Wednesday.

“We can’t afford to slip up in any way; we need to be perfect in all senses to get the result we want.”

McGuire was impressed by the quality of the Ukrainian side in his first experience of European club football, highlighting their attacking threat in particular.

He added: “I think individual qualities in that team were outstanding. I think the striker and the winger were really good.

“I knew they’d be decent players, I knew they’d be a decent team, and they were, but a few top, top players that can hurt us on Wednesday.”

#2201. Three games, three goals, three wins: Midfield maverick stars again as Norwich City thrash Derby County

Norwich City cruised past Derby County with much of the hard work done by half time. NCFC were 3-0 up at the break, and Jovon Makama lashed home a stunning striker to seal the victory in the second half.

It was another strong team performance for the Canaries, as displayed by the fact there were four different goalscorers. However, one man who stood out and got himself on the scoresheet once again was attacking midfielder Paris Maghoma.

Maghoma had Rams midfielder Alex Mowatt biting on every dummy before he fired home from outside the box for the Canaries’ second goal of the night. It made it three goals in three consecutive wins for the maverick playmaker, who looks to be back at his best.

Maghoma made an impression early on in his Norwich City career, scoring in his first starts in the FA Cup and Championship after joining in January. His trickery and flair has frustrated even manager Philippe Clement at times, but it isn’t easy to curtail someone as expressive and skilful as the 25-year-old.

The attacking midfielder was influential in the Derby County win. Alongside his goal, Maghoma created one chance and one big chance, also completed five passes into the final third (Fotmob).

Maghoma had only started two Championship games before his recent three-game scoring and starting run. His per 90 stats show just how impactful he has been when on the pitch though, offering a creative streak and valuable abilities in progressing the ball through passes and dribbling.

Across his 442 league minutes, the NCFC ace is averaging 2.44 chances created, 6.11 line-breaking passes, 57.83 touches and a 60% dribble success rate per 90. His three goals from 10 shots and just 0.87 xG shows how clinical he has been when given an opportunity at goal too – although that does beg the question whether such goalscoring form will continue (all stats via Fotmob).

Maghoma has been a standout player in Norwich City’s three-game winning run, and there will be confidence that he can continue in this vein. However, both he and the entire team face a challenge in the effort to maintain their form.

The last three games have been against Derby County, Watford and Charlton Athletic – three of the league’s worst form teams. If NCFC are to keep pushing up the table and come good on their promotion ambitions, they have to maintain these high standards against tougher opposition.

A trip to Michael Skubala’s Bristol City marks a step up for the Canaries, but it is another winnable match. It would be a real morale boost to enter the upcoming international break off the back of four wins, and Maghoma’s recent form indicates he will have a key part to play in continuing the run.

#2200. Birmingham City's £2.2m signing has just given Chris Davies a major headache

Birmingham City manager Chris Davies has hailed the influence of Max Bird as his side made it four wins from five Championship matches with a convincing 3-0 success over Millwall at St. Andrew's @ Knighthead Park.

Having returned to winning ways with a 3-1 success at Lincoln City on Saturday, Birmingham continued their unbeaten run on home turf, with all three goals coming before the half-hour mark.

Alex Cochrane netted his second in as many games with a powerful drive after just 46 seconds, replicating his fine finish against the Lions 12 months ago in the process, before Bird was given acres of space to drill his first goal for the club home on 16 minutes.

Jay Stansfield then netted his second of the season 13 minutes later from Bird's quick thinking, allowing Birmingham to cruise through the second period and up to second in the Championship ahead of Wednesday's remaining fixtures.

Much was made of how Blues were going to perform this campaign given a quieter summer transfer window, as Bird was just one of seven arrivals in B9, joining from Bristol City for a reported £2.2m.

Tuesday's encounter was also his first start since moving from the West Country side, and he certainly made quite the impression on Davies and those in the stands.

Jude Bellingham once named three unlikely Birmingham City players as his football heroes

Davies' team selection certainly generated interest, with Bird replacing August Priske in the starting lineup, whilst the Dane was omitted from the squad altogether due to a minor knock.

As such, the 26-year-old featured in the '10' role behind Stansfield, and such a decision paid dividends as Birmingham swept Alex Neil's team aside from the get-go.

Having assisted Demarai Gray in the 4-0 rout over Preston North End, Bird marked his full debut with a remarkable performance and his first goal, with Davies paying compliments to the midfielder's 'football brain' post-match.

"As a coach it’s lovely to work with really bright, intelligent players," said Davies. “In little exercises and training sessions you do, he’s tuned in straight away. He knows exactly what tactically you’re wanting."

“I think that’s a real midfield player. He’s thinking about the game, the positioning, the space and everything else," he added. “He’s played as a six, an eight and a 10 so he’s got a real understanding of all the roles. He’s an intelligent lad."

“What he’s got as well is legs. You can be intelligent and technical but maybe not have the other side, but he can do that side of it as well and that’s critical in this team because of how aggressive we are in the press.”

Bird's technical quality at Championship level has been known for many years, having excelled for both the Robins and Derby County before returning to Birmingham this summer, having spent time in the club's academy setup.

Despite sustaining an early-season leg injury, the playmaker has already won plenty of fans over with his contributions.

"If last night's performance from Max Bird is just the start, I cannot wait to watch more of him. Top drawer of a first start for the club," said one thrilled Bluenose.

Another stated: "Blues were so dominant in that first half. Several stand out performances last night, but Max Bird was unplayable at times. If we can keep him fit, we’ve got a serious player on our hands."

Blues fans, did you expect such an immediate impact from Max Bird? Comment below!

"Max Bird was unbelievable today. Haven’t seen a midfielder run a game like that for a while. I didn’t realise how much of a powerful runner he is. When he gets going he looks impossible to tackle," wrote another extremely impressed supporter.

Another summation of the midfielder's impact was: "Max Bird is like a conductor with the three dancers playing off him."

Last season was one of mixed fortunes for Birmingham, as despite finishing 10th after sauntering to the League One title, more was expected on the outside given Knighthead's continued investment.

However, Davies' side are certainly much more complete and efficient this term, and with goals and assists coming from all across the squad, they have become a force to be reckoned with.

Although there are still many games to go, the fact they have reached the Championship's automatic promotion places for the first time under the 41-year-old will be a major confidence boost ahead of Saturday's eye-catching clash with Swansea City.

#2199. Sheffield Wednesday transfer update emerges as Dave Challinor faces tricky situation

Sheffield Wednesday remain in discussions with the EFL over what they can do in the January window, although it seems unlikely Dave Challinor will be in a position to make major changes to the squad.

It was a remarkably hectic summer for the Owls after Arise Capital Partners completed their takeover of the club at the end of the previous campaign.

A major squad overhaul followed, but Wednesday were under EFL restrictions in terms of what they could do, so the squad was packed out with loan signings and free transfers.

Nevertheless, they still boast a lot of quality by League One standards, but an inconsistent start to the season meant Henrik Pedersen paid the price as he lost his job.

The Yorkshire outfit moved quickly to bring in Dave Challinor as his successor, and the former Stockport boss is preparing for his first game in charge at Oldham on Sunday in the FA Cup.

Whilst he will be keen on a cup run, the league will be the priority, and Challinor will hope to take Wednesday back to the Championship at the first attempt.

In normal circumstances, the new boss would also have one eye on the January window, where he may want to make a few tweaks to the group.

Yet, as outlined above, the situation at Wednesday is different due to the restrictions, and the Sheffield Star has stated that the club are ‘close to the limit’ in terms of what they can spend.

FLW looks at who entertains the most, and the least, in League One

And, speaking to the same outlet, sporting director Simon Wilson admitted they still don’t know exactly how they will be able to back Challinor in the New Year.

“We’re not 100 per cent sure exactly what it is. We’re constantly in dialogue with the league around the rules and the limitations. We obviously have the ability to change the squad, as anyone does. The window is open and business can be done.

“At this moment in time, Dave has just come into the building, he needs a bit of time to assess the squad and get a feel for which players are going to be the most useful and where we have areas of need. Then we’ll work into the window from that point.”

Obviously, this is not ideal for Wednesday, as most clubs will already be drawing up plans for January, and whilst the Owls may have players in mind, they still don’t know who they can bring in.

Barnsley 0-1 Sheffield Wednesday (after extra time), Wembley, 29 May 2023. Type the surnames of Darren Moore's starting XI. Every player you get drops onto the pitch.

You have 90 seconds. Surnames are enough.

Josh Windass headed in Lee Gregory's cross in the 123rd minute to send the Owls up.

But, Challinor won’t be too worried about that, as he will be focused on improving the players he has inherited.

There is still a lot of talent in the Wednesday squad right now, and, to the credit of the new owners, they have done a lot with the restrictions they were under.

Will Sheffield Wednesday win promotion under Dave Challinor this season? Let us know in the comments below.

So, Challinor will believe he can still get results from the current crop, and it will be interesting to see which players benefit from his appointment.

Then, when January does come around, you can be sure that Wednesday will do what they can, but it seems likely that major changes aren’t on the cards, but that shouldn’t be too much of a problem.
