#2198. James Bree incident in West Brom v Southampton match sparks reaction

Southampton full-back James Bree has sparked a strong reaction on social media following his side's 1-1 draw with West Bromwich Albion on Tuesday night.

With the scores level in B71 after Samuel Edozie equalised early in the second period following Isaac Price's first-half opener, it has been debated whether the Saints defender successfully deceived referee, Josh Smith, who stopped the game for a head injury.

Both West Brom and Southampton have started the Championship season in impressive form, with Tonda Eckert's side still sitting amongst the division's early pacesetters despite being deducted four points due to the Spygate scandal.

Those who are a part of the South Coast club have, this season, been playing the role of pantomime villains, and that was certainly the case at The Hawthorns for those backing the hosts, who are now unbeaten in six successive matches.

Who are the biggest wind-up specialists in the EFL Championship right now? Football League World takes a deep dive...

In what was a pulsating encounter, it is fair to say that Albion were more than deserving of their half-time lead, with Saints' attack leaving Max O'Leary untroubled, before Edozie's 53rd-minute leveller certainly gave Eckert's side a fresh impetus.

West Brom still showed signs that they could take all three points, and after a spell of attacking promise, Bree was seen on the ground without movement, leaving Smith to stop the game, although the Southampton physios were swiftly waved away by the full-back.

Asked about the incident post-match, Morrison stated: "I think, because the pressure was coming from us, he tried to stop the game.

Asked whether Bree should have face further punishment, the Baggies boss added: "We've asked for consistency, so let's hope it comes."

West Brom, of course, saw Aune Heggebo banned for two matches for the deception of a match official in August after his handballed goal on the opening day against Norwich City, which was the first time a player had been banned for such wrongdoing in English football.

As such, Baggies fans are calling for Bree to face a similar punishment.

"Faking head injuries is becoming all too common and requires stronger action from officials. If staying down holding your head resulted in an automatic 3 minutes off the pitch while checked over by medics, I suspect we’ll suddenly see a lot less of it," was the opinion of one Albion fan.

Another Baggies supporter wrote: "Disgraceful behaviour, so obvious what he was doing before ref blew his whistle & then waved his hands to say he don’t need any medical attention so he don’t go off. Ref was very poor all night tho imo. Standard EFL ref."

West Brom and Southampton fans, what are your thoughts on the incident? Comment below!

"Absolutely appalling behaviour - so clear and obvious - should have been booked and EFL need to take immediate action for the credibility of football," was another strong verdict on the matter.

"It shouldn’t be done, but it literally happens in every game of professional football," another comment read.

There is, ultimately, no proof that the Baggies would have definitely restored their advantage, but given the punishment which Heggebo received two months ago, the stance of those associated with the West Midlands club is hardly a surprise.

Bree's decision to go down isn't the only incident which has been heavily criticised in recent days too, with Liverpool legend, Jamie Carragher, slamming Alexis Mac Allister's decision to 'feign' injury after the Argentinian midfielder brushed heads with Arsenal's Noni Madueke in the Gunners' 1-0 win at Anfield.

Five players, five careers. Name them from the clubs they played for.

Each day there are five current or former EFL players to identify. For each one you’ll see their senior clubs in the order they played for them. Loan spells are left out.

You get four guesses per player. Every wrong guess unlocks a clue: first their position, then their nationality, then their initials.

Get it first time for 4 points, then 3, 2 and 1. The best possible score is 20. A new set of players arrives at midnight.

Former referee, Keith Hackett, has also called on the Football Association to take retrospective action on Bree's actions, also adding that Smith should have brandished a yellow card to the defender for "unsporting behaviour."

At present, though, it remains to be seen what action, if any, will be taken.

We want to hear from you. Share your perspective in the comments below, and please keep the conversation respectful.

#2197. Dowman weaves his magic and new signing shines as Arsenal hit ground running

Teenage sensation Max Dowman was the star of Arsenal’s first pre-season match, as he scored one goal and assisted another in a 4-1 victory over Girona.

Dowman, 16, was joined on the scoresheet by new signing Christos Tzolis, who struck with a low effort in his first game since his £34m move from Belgian side Club Brugge.

Established attackers Kai Havertz and Gabriel Jesus also scored for the Premier League champions, who were largely comfortable against opposition from the Spanish second tier.

Here are four things Telegraph Sport learnt from the match:

It was this time last year that Dowman first announced his remarkable talent to the wider world. Then only 15, he sparkled in pre-season and made it clear to Mikel Arteta that he was ready to impact matches at the highest level.

A year on, Dowman is now an established first-team player. He is the youngest ever Premier League winner and the competition’s youngest ever scorer, and he looks set to make even more of a mark this season.

In this friendly against Girona, Dowman created Arsenal’s opening goal with a gorgeous defence-splitting pass for Havertz. He did so after receiving the ball under pressure and spinning into space. Dowman then scored Arsenal’s third with a powerful low drive from the edge of the box.

Dowman is in competition with Bukayo Saka and Noni Madueke for a place on the right wing, which means this summer represents a huge opportunity for the teenager. After playing for England at the World Cup, Saka and Madueke will both miss most of pre-season.

Dowman, therefore, has a serious chance of going into the new campaign as the starting right-winger. The Community Shield on August 16 must be a target in his mind.

“We know what he’s capable of doing,” Arteta said. “We want to be more consistent in terms of the performances and the actions that he can deliver, but I think today he had a really good game.”

Arsenal are close to completing a deal for Newcastle United captain Bruno Guimarães but, for now, their only outfield signing of the summer has been Tzolis. This was the Greek winger’s first match in front of supporters and he immediately demonstrated why Arsenal were willing to pay £34m to buy him from Club Brugge.

With Tzolis, it is all about the final product. Goals and assists. He struck 22 times for Club Brugge last season, and registered 29 assists.

How did he produce such impressive numbers? The answer could be seen in his first-half goal against Girona. Receiving the ball on the left wing, Tzolis quickly accelerated towards the penalty area and unleashed a low shot. It was perhaps a more direct approach than Arsenal would usually have seen from Leandro Trossard, the player Tzolis has replaced, and it caught Girona off-guard as the ball deflected into the net.

“I’m very pleased with him,” Arteta said. “First of all, the way he has adapted to the club, to the team. The connection he’s already generating with the boys. I think you’re going to love the player.

“A player who’s very direct. He’s got the goal between the eyes. He has a lot of similarities with Leo [Trossard] in a lot of the things that he can do and the spaces he can occupy. And then the work rate that he has... He’s a boy that comes with so much hunger. He wants to prove himself, it’s a dream for him. And we are here to help him.”

Havertz was one of the few Arsenal players who benefited from playing at the World Cup. His injury issues mean that, unlike most of his team-mates, he did not end the 2025-26 season in a state of exhaustion.

After returning to the pitch in the spring, Havertz enjoyed an impressive end to the campaign for Arsenal. He then performed well at the World Cup, scoring three goals for Germany.

He remains one of Arteta’s favourite players, not least because of his versatility. He started in attack in the crucial end-of-season games in May, but played in midfield against Girona. His low finish, from Dowman’s pass, represented his eighth goal in his last 12 matches for club and country.

Girona’s goal, scored by Arnau Martínez, was perhaps the only alarming moment of this comfortable pre-season victory. Martínez was unmarked from a left-wing corner when he powered a header into Arsenal’s net.

For a group of players who pride themselves on their set-piece prowess, this was a disappointing moment. It also perhaps showed Arsenal’s reliance on their two first-choice centre-backs, William Saliba and Gabriel Magalhães, when they are defending crosses into their box.

Gabriel arrived at Arsenal’s pre-season training camp a few days ago, so he should be in good shape by the start of the new campaign. Saliba, though, will be missing for months with a back problem.

Without Saliba’s height and power, will Arsenal be as effective from set-pieces in the opening chunk of the campaign? Coventry City, Arsenal’s opponents on the first night of the season, will undoubtedly look to test the champions in these situations.

The reigning Premier League champions are handed the Costa Brava Trophy, which is half-heartedly lifted into the air by White. There will be far bigger trophies on offer to Arsenal in the upcoming campaign.

Arsenal have cruised to a routine 4-1 win over Girona, with Havertz, Tzolis, Dowman and Gabriel Jesus all finding the net. Arteta will be delighted with his side’s professionalism and ruthlessness.

Meslier takes too long on his goal kick, gifting a corner to Girona. However, the delivery from the hosts is so poor as it flies harmlessly out of play. That sums up Girona’s difficult evening.

There is another round of substitutions for both sides.

Once again, Meslier makes a pivotal stop on his Arsenal debut. Martin clips an exquisite pass over Arsenal’s defence to the onrushing Ruiz, who is through on goal. The striker takes the chance first time, but Meslier is there to make another crucial save.

Arsenal’s makeshift line-up, which is full of Hale End graduates, is holding firm, with Girona evidently struggling for attacking inspiration. If Arsenal can see out this victory without any injuries, then it would have panned out exactly how Arteta would have wanted.

Girona carelessly give possession away in defence, allowing Nelson to dribble towards the penalty area. The winger floats a cross into the box, which is met by O’Neill, but the forward’s lofted header hits the top of the bar.

Will that lead to more sustained vulnerability over the opening chunk of the season?

Girona have sent a host of players out to warm up. They’re playing in their fourth pre-season match, with their league campaign due to start on August 16 against Leganes.

That was a straightforward half for Arsenal. Arteta will be pleased with Havertz’s showing in his 33 minutes on the pitch. After missing so much of last season through injury, it has been a good summer for Havertz so far. He scored three goals in Arsenal’s final six games of 2025/26, and then netted four times for Germany in June.

The 2009-born playmaker was Arsenal’s standout player in that first half. Dowman’s confidence and class on the ball has been brilliant, with his expertly-crafted assist for Havertz’s opener an obvious highlight.

Tzolis registered 22 goals and 29 assists for Club Brugge last season. He is an end-product machine, and that goal was a little indication of how he racks up such eye-watering numbers. Since their goal, Arsenal have assumed real authority of this encounter and look like the far superior side.

Girona captain Martinez slams a powerful long-range effort at goal, but it fizzes wide of the bottom corner. Kepa seemed to have it covered regardless.

With England wingers Bukayo Saka and Noni Madueke not returning until later in pre-season, Dowman has a chance to take ownership of the right wing position ahead of the Community Shield. His assist for Kai Havertz, a lovely measured pass after an excellent piece of skill in midfield, was a sign that Dowman means business.

Dowman drifts inside and pops up in the right channel, wriggling past Moreno, before threading a delightful pass through to Havertz. One-on-one, the German calmly slots a close-range effort into the bottom corner, giving Arsenal a well-deserved lead. So much credit must go to Dowman, who has started this game excellently.

White leads Arsenal out onto the pitch to face Girona, who boast the likes of Van de Beek, Gil and Moreno in their starting XI.

Talking earlier this week, Arsenal boss Mikel Arteta sent out a determined message to other clubs by outlining their ambitious transfer plans.

“A lot is happening,” Arteta said. “We all know about the context of this transfer window. From ownership to the board, the sporting director and myself, we know that we want to take this club to a different level.

“That is going to require a better squad, better individuals. We have identified where we have opportunities to grow and to improve and to evolve our game and what is going to be needed to achieve that. Hopefully very soon we can start to put things in a very concrete way.”

Arteta also believes that last season’s Premier League title has served as added motivation for his squad to improve and hit new heights.

“This has to be the start and this has to be the standard,” he said. “Excellence has to be our standard and this has to drive to attack the future. The way we behave daily with more and more determination and ambition, because we’ve shown that we’ve got it. Now we have to show that we belong to this level and we want to increase and take this football club to a different dimension.”

It had been a relatively quiet transfer window for Arsenal, who have recruited just goalkeeper Illan Meslier and winger Christos Tzolis.

However, Arsenal are now moving very bullishly, closing on Newcastle United midfielder Bruno Guimarães, while also targeting Real Madrid’s Vinícius Júnior.

Sam Dean has the full breakdown of a potential deal for the Real Madrid star and how Arsenal are prepared to continue flexing their muscles in the transfer market in what would be one of the biggest moves in Premier League history.

It was January 2025, with Arsenal earning a hard-fought 2-1 comeback victory in the Champions League courtesy of first-half goals from Jorginho and Ethan Nwaneri.

Since this European encounter, Girona have been on a seriously downward trajectory, enduring lowly 16th and 19th finishes in La Liga, with the latter ensuring relegation to the Segunda Division, where they’ll play in the upcoming campaign.

August 5: Arsenal vs Real Betis (Dublin, Ireland)

August 9: Arsenal vs Borussia Dortmund (London, England)

August 12: Arsenal vs Como (London, England)

August 16: Arsenal vs Manchester City (Cardiff, Wales)

Mikel Arteta’s side will then begin their defence of the Premier League title on August 21 when they host newly-promoted Coventry City on August 21.

Arsenal are closing in on one of the statement signings of the summer, with Newcastle United midfielder Bruno Guimarães getting closer to joining the Premier League holders.

This deal means that Christian Norgaard is expected to leave and seal a move to Everton for around £7m.

As previously reported by Telegraph Sport, Guimarães has been Arsenal’s top target for weeks. It is believed that he will cost around £80m.

Unlike other Premier League heavyweights, Arsenal have kept their pre-season tour relatively local with a selection of games in Spain, Ireland and England, before they face Manchester City in the FA Community Shield on August 16 at the Millennium Stadium in Cardiff.

Arsenal beat League One side MK Dons 3-0 in a behind-closed-doors friendly on July 25 at the Sobha Realty Training Centre, thanks to goals from Reiss Nelson, Ethan Nwaneri and Ceadach O’Neill.

Mikel Arteta’s men will play a wounded Girona, who suffered relegation from the top flight of Spanish football last season due to a 19th-place finish.

Kick-off is at 19:00, with team news arriving shortly.

James Penrice was welcomed into the Scotland fold with a cheeky message from Rangers team-mate Nico Raskin after earning his first senior international call-up.

The 27-year-old left-back has been selected by Sébastien Pocognoli for this month’s Nations League double-header against North Macedonia and Switzerland.

🏴󠁧󠁢󠁳󠁣󠁴󠁿 A first @ScotlandNT call-up for James Penrice! 💙 James joins teammates Findlay Curtis and Liam Kelly in the squad for the upcoming UEFA Nations League fixtures. 🎙️ Fresh off the training pitch, @RangersTV and Nico Raskin caught up with James following the news. https://t.co/jMukr0qH2n

Raskin then joked about Belgian boss Pocognoli’s decision to select the Rangers defender. He said: “Well-deserved. I always knew Belgian managers have good eyes to see players!”

#2195. West Ham have given Cesar Peixoto a major Wolves headache after Nuno decision

West Ham and Wolves started the Championship season as the two firm favourites for automatic promotion.

Yet, it’s fair to say neither side has hugely impressed in the opening months of the campaign, even if they are both certainly in the hunt to finish in the top two.

Despite their decent positions, the Hammers have seen enough to make a change in the dugout, with Scott Parker replacing Nuno Espírito Santo as head coach.

That shows just how important winning promotion is to the Irons, and Wolves are in a similar boat.

Firstly, it should be said that there’s absolutely no suggestion Peixoto could lose his job, and Wolves will rightly point out that they are ahead of West Ham in the table.

Some will say it’s extremely harsh that Nuno has been sacked with his team just four points away from second, so it would be on another level if Peixoto was dismissed, as Wanderers are third, and just two points behind Swansea going into the midweek fixtures.

Nevertheless, there’s no denying that Peixoto still hasn’t got the backing of all Wolves fans, which is largely down to their inconsistent performances.

There is no clear pattern of play from the Portuguese head coach, and his constant changes to the XI have been baffling.

As well as that, some fans are not happy with his preference for certain players and his substitutions, which is why chants of ‘you don’t know what you’re doing’ were aimed at Peixoto in the recent game against Watford - which Wolves were winning at the time!

The challenge for Peixoto will be to replicate what Nuno did at Molineux by taking the club back to the Premier League.

The circumstances are very different though, so the reality is that even if they do win promotion, Peixoto will not receive the adulation of his former Porto teammate.

Nuno’s appointment at Wolves in 2017 was the start of a remarkable journey for the Midlands outfit, during which time they hit heights that few thought were possible.

As a result, Nuno is viewed as a legend at Molineux, as he built the best team seen in decades, as Wolves returned to the European stage and regularly bloodied the noses of the best clubs in the country.

Plus, he also bought into what the city was about, and he had a special bond with the supporters.

Following on from that, it feels that any Wolves manager since is, perhaps unfairly, compared to Nuno, even if there is an understanding that the ambition of the owners is nowhere near what it once was.

So, with news of his sacking, it’s inevitable that some fans will call for Nuno to return to the place they feel is ‘home’ for the ex-Nottingham Forest chief.

Of course, that won’t be the view of every fan, but Nuno’s departing message in 2021 was that this is ‘not a goodbye, it’s see you soon’, suggesting that he too would be open to returning at some point.

Despite his mixed start to this season with West Ham, Nuno would be seen as a coup for any Championship club, so if Peixoto does struggle at any point, then it’s not hard to imagine that calls for the former manager to return will grow, especially as he is available.

You do have sympathy for Peixoto, because this is none of his doing, and it’s giving him a headache and distraction that he doesn’t need just months into his Wolves career.

Furthermore, it’s not like he is actively disliked by Wolves fans, more that he hasn’t fully won them over, whilst some will be delighted at their league position.

But, rightly or wrongly, Nuno’s availability will naturally add a bit more pressure, and it’s undoubtedly going to be brought up to Peixoto at some point.

Will Wolves and West Ham both win promotion this season? Let us know in the comments below.

However, that doesn’t have to be a bad thing, and, if he embraces the pressure, it will allow him to try and build his own relationship with the supporters.

Ultimately, they both want the same thing - for Wolves to reach the Premier League, and preferably by playing stylish football.

So, instead of Nuno’s shadow lurking in the background negatively, he must use it as motivation to make his own mark at Molineux, even if it’s unlikely he will manage to match his legacy.

We want to hear from you. Share your perspective in the comments below, and please keep the conversation respectful.

#2194. Jake Cooper interview after Millwall's loss to Birmingham City sparks reaction

Millwall captain Jake Cooper has sparked a reaction through his post-match assessment of the Lions' 3-0 defeat against Birmingham City at St. Andrew's @ Knighthead Park on Tuesday night.

Having romped to a 4-1 success over lowly Derby County on Saturday, there was hope that Alex Neil's side could continue an upsurge in the Championship standings.

Instead, they were the side who found themselves three goals behind in very little time, with all of Birmingham's strikes from Alex Cochrane, Max Bird and Jay Stansfield coming ahead of the half-hour mark.

Blues climbed into the automatic promotion places as a result, with Chris Davies' men winning four of their last five matches, scoring 14 goals during that timeframe.

Having finished third last season, Millwall have started the current campaign indifferently, winning five of their opening 14 encounters, whilst a sixth loss of the campaign saw them drop to 13th.

Cooper, 31, knows the Championship inside out, with his outing on Tuesday taking him nine away from 450 appearances in the division for the Lions and his previous club, Reading.

Although Birmingham found themselves cruising to victory by the time Bird made it 2-0 on 16 minutes, it was Millwall who created the first-half's only 'big chance' whilst the hosts still forged 15 attempts before the interval.

Speaking to Millwall's in-house media post-match, Cooper believed that the scoreline didn't reflect the overall balance of the game.

"Obviously, the first feeling is disappointment, like you say," he said. "I don't think they did enough to score three goals against us.

"I think we had some good opportunities to get back in the game, at important times, that we couldn't take.

"It's important at this level, both boxes are what makes the difference. They were clinical and we, unfortunately, were lacking in that area today," Cooper added.

The summer recruit was key to Blues' fourth win in five Championship games

Davies' side have developed a habit of putting those who visit St. Andrew's to the sword, with it being the third successive home outing in which Birmingham have netted at least three goals.

Millwall only tested Ryan Allsop with two of their 16 attempts, though, which tells its own story by and large, and Cooper's assessment certainly baffled some of the home support.

Blues and Millwall fans, what are your thoughts on Jake Cooper's assessment? Comment below

"How can he say Birmingham didn’t do enough to score their 3 goals? It was a joy to watch how fluid Birmingham were. Game was done inside 20 odd mins," backed up the general consensus from Blues fans.

There were also some Millwall fans not on board with Cooper's stance, with one stating: "lol they looked like scoring every attack in that first half. Could have been 5 or 6."

If Birmingham's fans were bemused by Cooper's stance, then the likelihood is they will also have felt the same way when reading Neil's post-match thoughts.

"The fact we have created the chances is a good thing because we looked threatening, but the lack of clinical edge in the final third was a big problem for us," he said.

"Goals change games. The lack of discipline in the first half didn't help us, albeit they have had four shots and three of them go in the back of our net.

"We are really disappointed that we didn't manage to build on the weekend. It is disappointing the manner we have lost the game."

The style of play at the Riverside Stadium has been completely transformed within said timeframe, and across the opening three months of 2026/27, one man has finally solved the club's biggest achilles heel from last season's final weeks - the ability to score goals.

That is, of course, none other than Will Lankshear, who was one of several high-profile names to have moved to Teesside throughout the summer, doing so from Tottenham Hotspur.

The 21-year-old was no stranger to the Championship at the time of his initial £10m switch from the North London club, but his remarkable adjustment to life at the Riverside could be rewarded with the biggest compliment.

Spurs sold Will Lankshear to Boro in the summer, but, they have clauses written into the contract to protect their position in the future.

The aforementioned deal could still rise as high as £20m with add-ons, meaning Spurs can still benefit financially through their academy graduate's success.

However, right now, no one is benefiting more from Lankshear's goalscoring prowess and all-round game than Hellberg, with his recent double against Charlton Athletic taking the 21-year-old's tally to 13 goals in as many Championship games.

There were concerns over his fitness for Wednesday night's clash at Wrexham, but after being given the all-clear, it has been revealed that a senior England scout will oversee Lankshear's performance on Thomas Tuchel's behalf, with the Three Lions boss set to confirm his latest squad on Friday morning.

“Three strikers, how many strikers do you want in the squad? Three strikers I think are enough. To answer about the player in Middlesbrough, no (regrets)."

Shumail Sajid writes about Manchester United for Read Man Utd and Crystal Palace for Read Crystal Palace, with occasional pieces on other Premier League clubs. He has also written for FanSided's Red Devils Dispatch, Yardbarker, Anfield Central and The Sports Side.

Manchester United and Tottenham Hotspur return from the international break with plenty to prove when they meet at Old Trafford on Saturday.

Michael Carrick’s side have won just once in their last four domestic matches since beating Ipswich 5-2. A Carabao Cup defeat to Brighton was followed by a loss to 10-man Manchester City, before Manchester United drew with Everton and Fulham. Matheus Cunha’s late equaliser at Fulham rescued a point, but Manchester United still sit 12th.

Roberto De Zerbi’s side are bottom of the Premier League with only two points from their opening five games. Spurs have failed to score in four of those matches, while defeats against Aston Villa and Newcastle have added to the pressure.

Michael Carrick has named his starting eleven for the clash at Old Trafford, with Kobbie Mainoo and Youri Tielemans partnering in midfield as United look to get their season back on track.

Senne Lammens starts in goal, with Leny Yoro, Lisandro Martinez, Harry Maguire and Luke Shaw forming the back four. Carrick has opted for Mainoo and Tielemans in the middle, with Amad Diallo, Bruno Fernandes and Matheus Cunha tasked with supporting Bryan Mbeumo up front.

Leny Yoro had a brilliant international break where he made his debut for France. His performance on debut was enough for Zidane to praise the debutant.

Amad, after missing the start of the season with an injury, returns straightaway to the team.

Lammens; Yoro, Martinez, Maguire, Shaw; Mainoo, Tielemans; Amad, Bruno Fernandes, Mbeumo; Cunha.

United need a response after a difficult run, but Tottenham arrive under pressure of their own. With both sides desperate for points, the starting lineups set the stage for an important afternoon at Old Trafford.

#2189. Barry Bannan reacts as Ali Al-Hamadi drops Sheffield Wednesday message

Sheffield Wednesday striker Ali Al-Hamadi has taken to social media to reflect on his start to life at Hillsborough, and team-mate Barry Bannan has reacted to his post.

Al-Hamadi was one of 18 new signings to join Wednesday this summer as part of the club's rebuild under new owner David Storch, but it is fair to say his loan move from Ipswich Town has not gone as well as he would have hoped so far.

It has been an inconsistent start to life back in League One for Wednesday, with the South Yorkshire outfit currently sitting ninth in the table, two points from the play-off places, after winning just two of their last nine league games.

After parting company with Henrik Pedersen last month, the Owls appointed former Stockport County boss Dave Challinor as their new manager this week, and the 51-year-old is set to take charge for the first time in Sunday's FA Cup tie at Oldham Athletic.

However, while Challinor will be keen to run the rule over his new squad over the coming weeks, he may be without Al-Hamadi for the opening games of his tenure after he suffered a fresh injury blow.

Al-Hamadi is yet to open his account for Wednesday since his summer arrival, and injuries have limited him to just eight appearances so far, with his only start coming in the 2-0 defeat to Doncaster last month which proved to be Pedersen's final game.

After missing a few games earlier in the season with a foot problem, Al-Hamadi was not in the squad for Sunday's 1-1 draw with Blackpool due to a new injury, which manager Matt Hamshaw revealed could keep him out for "a number of weeks".

Unfortunately for Al-Hamadi, he has had his fair share of injury woes in recent years, particularly during his loan spell at Luton Town last season, where he scored just one goal and provided one assist in 14 appearances.

Al-Hamadi would have been to get a consistent run of games under his belt at Hillsborough and establish himself in the Wednesday team, but despite finding himself in the treatment room once again, it seems the Iraq international is determined to bounce back from his latest setback.

"Frustratingly, it has been stop-start the last few weeks for me personally," Al-Hamadi wrote on Instagram on Tuesday.

"Working as hard as ever to stay on that pitch, help the team and reach our goals for this season."

Al-Hamadi was inundated with support after his candid reflection on his time at Wednesday, with the post attracting over 16,600 likes at the time of writing, and among those was his Owls team-mate Barry Bannan.

Al-Hamadi has proven himself to be a prolific scorer in the EFL previously during his spell in League Two with AFC Wimbledon, but he has struggled to produce his best form since departing Plough Lane for Ipswich for a fee of just over £1 million almost three years ago.

Despite his injury problems at Luton last season, it is easy to see why Wednesday took a gamble on Al-Hamadi this summer, but as he continues to be plagued by fitness issues, his loan stint at Hillsborough is in danger of turning into another flop.

Should Ali Al-Hamadi be a regular starter for Sheffield Wednesday under Dave Challinor once he returns from injury? Tell us in the comments below!

With Challinor taking over this week, Al-Hamadi would no doubt have been keen to show the new Owls boss what he is capable of, but it appears he will be unavailable for the early stages of his reign, which could allow others to move ahead of him in the pecking order.

Manchester United and Tottenham Hotspur returned from the international break with plenty to prove after a disastrous start to the season.

United arrived with just one win, while Tottenham came to Old Trafford without a win.

Both teams had half-chances in the first half but little to show for them. Tottenham had the better chances with chances for Dominic Solanke, Connor Gallagher and Kudus, but none could take advantage of them.

Manchester United came close in the first half to score after Bryan Mbeumo raced towards the goal on a counter-attack to find Amad. He had a difficult shot, and eventually the shot was too weak to cause any damage. The first-half display was met by boos from the Old Trafford crowd at half-time and during the first half as well.

Solanke had another chance at the start of the second half but put it over the top, amid a wrestle with Lisandro Martinez in the six-yard box. It was United, however, who started the second half with promise.

United failed to capitalize on their one-man advantage and seemed to sit on their 1-0 lead, but Solanke punished them with a header to level the game in injury time. The draw left United with just 6 points off their first six games. The result leaves United with their worst start in 40 years.

#2187. Unrest grows at Rotherham United after Tuesday night developments

Rotherham United exited the Jersey Mike's Trophy in rather disappointing fashion on Tuesday night, losing to Newcastle United's Under-21s at the AESSEAL New York Stadium.

Alex Bruce's side needed a pick-me-up in the midst of an eight-game winless run in all competitions, which has seen them slide down towards the relegation zone in League Two, and a chance to progress in the EFL Trophy would have helped provide that.

Instead, a rotated, yet still filled with experienced senior names such as Dominic Iorfa, Brandon Williams, Kian Spence and Kladi Lolos, squad put in a meek showing against an academy side, who ran away 1-0 victors and secured second place in Northern Group C.

Pick any two players. Send the code, and your mate enters it here to play the same pair.

It's not been the best of seasons so far for Rotherham back in League Two, but this particular result has soured opinion on Bruce, COO Paul Douglas and chairman Tony Stewart even further.

Rotherham weren't exactly banging on the door of Newcastle's Under-21s on Tuesday night, despite being behind for close to an hour. The Millers had just nine shots, despite their 65% possession, and the Magpies academy actually had more on target over the course of the game.

Rotherham fans have, understandably, voiced their displeasure at the performance and the result online, with the majority of the ire directed at the club's hierarchy.

One supporter posted a photo with the caption, "Stewart and Douglas, killing our club," while another tweeted, "Against a team of kids and we looked softer than them. The clubs rotten. Stewart out #rufc"

"Can Tony Stewart please exit the club now. Ruined his legacy, purely for his own ego. Stewart out," was also amongst the comments, as was "Only the trophy but wow, that might be a new low... That's saying something with the last few years."

Alex Bruce hasn't been without criticism, either, though. "Is this Bruce’s final game?" someone questioned. "Stewart out Bruce out McLaren out Douglas out anyone at board level out," was also commented.

Arguably more damaging, though, was the tweet stating that the South Yorkshire side were "dead and buried," and "the worst side in England."

It's not uncommon for sides to fall from League One to League Two and struggle in the division below. More often than not, those clubs are in for another relegation battle than they are a promotion one, and in Carlisle United and Forest Green Rovers' case, they fall through the trapdoor once again and into non-league.

Rotherham look dangerously close to being one of the next sides to do that, but you get the feeling that the writing has been on the wall for quite some time now.

The Millers have been one of the more unstable clubs in the EFL for a while, bouncing up and down from League Two to the Championship and then yo-yoing from the second and third tiers over the last decade.

Do you think Rotherham United could get relegated again this season? Let us know in the comments.

Since their double promotion to the second tier in 2014, Rotherham haven't spent more than three years in one division. Many felt that a lengthy period in League One could provide some stability, but it would only be two years before they fell back into the fourth tier.

Now, the scary possibility of falling out of the Football League is on the horizon, and a lot of Millers fans are numb to the rapid regression of the club in recent seasons.

It's been a real mess at Rotherham over the past 12 months, but it's been highlighted more so in the last six.

From Lee Clark calling out the players' commitment in the latter stages of the League One campaign last season, to the intriguing implementation of a Head of Football and then hiring Steve McClaren to take that role, to the long, drawn-out process of hiring a new head coach which landed at Alex Bruce's feet, it's not been smooth sailing.

AI has ranked the top 16 British football clubs and their hooligan firms.

Bruce came into the club just days before pre-season started, with just 14 senior players confirmed to be staying on. He's had to navigate wholesale changes in the squad and nurse a relegation hangover in what is his first EFL managerial gig.

And ultimately, the underlying numbers, especially going forward, haven't read awfully. But the new boss can't account for the effort his players put in on the pitch and some of the mindless decisions that his players have made, too.

Bruce may pay for the loss against Newcastle's kids with his job, but, ultimately, it would take a real miracle-maker to turn Rotherham's fortunes around and get the fanbase back onside.

Leeds are on level terms. A long throw from Ampadu out on the left is flicked on at the near post and Calvert-Lewin has the easiest of tap-ins at the back post. Liverpool were in cruise control at 2-0 up at the break but not have not been at it since half-time.

Justin is played in behind down the left channel and tries to pick out Calvert-Lewin in the centre of the box but Ndiaye steps in with a crucial interception.

Andoni Iraola is going to make a quadruple change. Elliott, Ramsay, Ndiaye and Tsimikas all come on. Szoboszlai is one of those to head off and hands Jones the armband.

Liverpool were much the better side in the first half but have not really been at the races since the break.

Leeds punish Kerkez’s error and get a goal back. Kerkez gifts the ball away inside his own half and Ampadu picks up not far outside the Liverpool penalty area. He spots the run of Aaronson to his left and slides it into the American, who takes one touch before sliding it underneath Mamardashvili and into the Liverpool net.

Wilson is fouled down Leeds’ right and he will take the free-kick. The Welshman clips it in and picks out Calvert-Lewin, whose header goes well wide of the target.

Calvert-Lewin gets a touch past Ndukwe just inside the Liverpool half and drives towards the Liverpool penalty area. It is difficult to know whether it is a shot or a cross from Calvert-Lewin and the ball goes wide of the far post. Bogle did make a run towards the back post and was hoping Calvert-Lewin would pick him out.

Liverpool negotiate a couple of long throws and a corner from Leeds in quick succession.

After Ndukwe’s pass inside his own half is intercepted, Justin decides to shoot from range but Mamardashvili easily saves.

Liverpool have made a number of changes at the break, with Chiesa, Jones, Gravenberch and Koumas all coming on. It takes an absolute age for Leeds to re-emerge, with Liverpool coming back out from the tunnel nearly ten minutes before Leeds. What on earth is going on in the Leeds dressing room at the break? This is ridiculous from Leeds.

The second half begins more than 20 minutes after the first ended. To be exact, 23 minutes is the gap. Calvert-Lewin is one of a few changes at half-time for Leeds, as is former Liverpool man Wilson. We are back under way in Chicago.

Jeremie 🔗 Flo 😍 pic.twitter.com/kxwhYA845Q

Andoni Iraola said before the game that Florian Wirtz would play 45 minutes in his first game of pre-season so we can expect him and Alexander Isak to come off at half-time.

Stateside Reds enjoying the action 🤩 pic.twitter.com/hfwaLmi8xB

Possession: Liverpool 60%-40% LeedsShots: 5-6Shots on target: 3-2Corners: 1-3

The first half is brought to an end and Liverpool take a 2-0 lead into the break courtesy of goals from Chambers and Wirtz.

Szoboszlai clips a delightful cross from the right all the way to the back post, aiming to pick out the run of Kerkez. A goal-kick is given, with the referee deciding the last touch came off Kerkez, but the Hungarian left-back is not happy with that decision. The replays prove why as the last touch came off Bogle.

There will be four minutes of added time at the end of this first half due to the Gudmundsson injury in particular.

Leeds have been forced into one change in this half and they might be forced into another here. As Wirtz scored, two Leeds players collided, which has resulted in Ampadu staying down and receiving treatment. The Leeds captain though does seem to be ok after receiving some treatment.

It is a lovely team goal from Liverpool to take them 2-0 up around five minutes before half-time. Nyoni’s flat ball out to the right side of the box is volleyed first time back across the box by Frimpong. Wirtz runs onto the ball and, from the penalty spot, slots the ball home past Cairns.

After Nyoni makes an interception inside his own half, Liverpool counter. The ball is shifted out to the left, where Ngumoha drives at Bogle. Ngumoha’s step-over takes him past Bogle inside the Leeds penalty area and he drives the ball across the six-yard box but no-one in a Liverpool shirt is on hand to tap it in. Should Isak have done a better job to get on the end of that one? Possibly.

Szoboszlai, who loves scoring free-kick stunners, blasts the free-kick into the wall.

Gudmundsson’s day is indeed over and is replaced by Bornauw, which could see a shift for Leeds.

Ngumoha is brought down by Bogle inches outside the Leeds penalty area out on the left. It was very, very close to being a penalty but was just outside the box. Before the free-kick will be taken, Leeds look like they will be forced into a change as Gudmundsson has gone down clutching at his right hamstring.

For the second time in a few minutes, Rodon steps in with a crucial interception. Wirtz slides a pass through into the Leeds box on the left to pick out the run of Ngumoha. Just as Ngumoha was getting his shot away from around eight yards out, Rodon slides in to intercept. However, the offside flag goes up against Ngumoha anyway.

Wirtz and Isak link up really well inside the Leeds half, with the latter putting a touch beyond one Leeds defender and runs towards the Leeds penalty area. However, Rodon steps in with a crucial interception to take it off Isak.

Nmecha scored from long range for Leeds the other day against Sunderland and he is not far off adding another long-range goal to his pre-season tally. His effort from just outside the box is dragged just wide of Mamardashvili’s right post.

Frimpong drives forward from inside his own half and takes Liverpool through the Leeds half before he is cynically pulled down by Tanaka, who is rightly booked. Sometimes in a pre-season friendly players might get away with that but this referee does not show mercy to Tanaka.

That is nearly a horror moment for Cairns in the Leeds goal. He rolls the ball out from his own box and Isak just about gets a touch on it but fortunately for Leeds it does not end in a horror show for Cairns.

Frimpong lays it across to Nyoni in a central position outside the box and the latter takes on the shot. Nyoni goes for accuracy over power and looks for the bottom corner but Cairns gets down to his left to make the save.

Chance for Leeds. Bogle whips in a cross from the right touchline and picks out the head of Nmecha, whose effort is saved well by Mamardashvili down to his right.

Liverpool hit the front in Chicago. Szoboszlai’s outswinger corner from the right is flicked on at the front post by Kerkez and is met by Chambers, who smashes home on the half volley into the Leeds net.

Liverpool counter from their own box after defending a long throw through Isak and Frimpong, whose cross from the right is deflected behind for the first corner of the game...

The pitch is not looking in the best condition, which perhaps is not a massive surprise when you consider that Chicago Fire played here last night. They beat Charlotte 2-1, with Robert Lewandowski scoring twice.

Gudmundsson is back to his feet after some treatment but is breathing quite heavily. It does appear that the Swedish wing-back should be fine to continue.

After Liverpool clear a Leeds long throw into the Liverpool penalty area, Gudmundsson goes down clutching at his lower back after an awkward landing and play is halted.

We are under way at Soldier Field. It is not too hot in Chicago today, with the temperature a touch over 20 degrees at kick-off.

Both sides emerge from the tunnel and we are just moments away from kick-off at Soldier Field in Chicago. You’ll Never Walk Alone rings around the stadium as the teams emerge.

Liverpool: Mamardashvili; Frimpong, Ndukwe, Chambers, Kerkez; Nyoni, Szoboszlai, Wirtz; Morrison, Isak, Ngumoha.Substitutes: Woodman, Davies, Chiesa, Jones, Elliott, Tsimikas, Gravenberch, Abe, Ramsay, Scanlon, McConnell, Koumas, Ndiaye, Wright, Sonni-Lambie.

Leeds: Cairns; Justin, Muharemovic, Rodon; Bogle, Ampadu, Stach, Tanaka, Gudmundsson; James, Nmecha.Substitutes: Mahady, Ombang, Lane, Lienou, Cresswell, Bornauw, Crew, Longstaff, Aaronson, Gnonto, Pickles, Wilson, Chadwick, Mills, Calvert-Lewin, Piroe.

There was a lot to take in, during those madcap 42 seconds, but it was a scene that showed the full extent of the issues Andoni Iraola must address.

First came a handshake with Curtis Jones that the midfielder, lost in red mist, barely acknowledged. It was not impressive, shrugging off a new manager like that, but as Iraola strode across the field at Yankee Stadium, after Liverpool’s 1-0 win over Wrexham on Wednesday, the action really began.

Jones squawked and jabbed at his arm. Dominik Szoboszlai bellowed back, arms stretched out so wide you could not help but notice. Next came Kostas Tsimikas throwing the captain’s armband on the floor, landing at Jones’s feet, as Giorgi Mamardashvili and Jeremie Frimpong looked on awkwardly.

The French defender, who has arrived from Rennes this summer, is not involved for Liverpool today and is yet to feature for his new club so far this pre-season as he is eased in after a shoulder injury days after his move to Liverpool was confirmed earlier this year.

Our team to take on Leeds United 🙌Watch the game LIVE on All Red Video:

Soldier Field in Chicago hosts an all-Premier League tie encounter as Liverpool take on Leeds as both sides bring their US tours to a close. Both Premier League encounters between these sides last season ended in draws; a 3-3 draw at Elland Road was followed up by a 0-0 stalemate at Anfield. The draw at Elland Road was immediately followed by Mohamed Salah speaking to the media, claiming he had been thrown under the bus.

It is a new era at Liverpool as former Bournemouth boss Andoni Iraola has replaced Arne Slot at Anfield. They kicked off the Iraola era in Nashville, Tennessee, with a 4-2 win over Sunderland, following that up with another victory in New York on Wednesday night, beating Wrexham 1-0, and will be aiming to make it three wins from three on their US tour.

“I think it [the US tour] has been really, really useful,” Iraola said in an interview on the official Liverpool website. Obviously, you spend a lot of time with the players, with the staff, you get all the information you can. And I think there is also an evolution, it has to be. We start to understand each other better, what we need to do. Every game, I hope we can get closer and closer and put ourselves in a position where the few players that still are not here start to train also, they are helped by the others.”

Virgil van Dijk and Cody Gakpo resumed training back on Merseyside whilst Alexis Mac Allister, Alisson and Victor Munoz are yet to return to training following their World Cup exploits. The trio of Florian Wirtz, Alexander Isak and Ryan Gravenberch are all set to feature for the first time this pre-season.

Leeds’ pre-season campaign began with a 3-2 loss to Championship Wrexham in Tampa, Florida before beating Sunderland 1-0 in New Jersey courtesy of a long-range strike from Lukas Nmecha. Former Liverpool man Harry Wilson joined Leeds on a free from Fulham this summer.

“Really tough but that is expected,” Wilson said. That is what pre-season is for, building up a base for when the season starts, making sure you are in the best physical position you can be to attack the season. It has been good. I played against them [Leeds] twice last year when I was at Fulham. Both games were really, really tough games.

“I think when the fans have got a good team to support, I think that [the atmosphere at Elland Road] goes up a notch. I think the size of the club was a massive part of me coming. Then speaking to the guys, the chairman, the sporting director, and seeing kind of the plans and the aims for the club, it is something I wanted to be a part of.”

#2185. Michael Carrick reacts to Man Utd boos after Tottenham draw

Shumail Sajid writes about Manchester United for Read Man Utd and Crystal Palace for Read Crystal Palace, with occasional pieces on other Premier League clubs. He has also written for FanSided's Red Devils Dispatch, Yardbarker, Anfield Central and The Sports Side.

Michael Carrick admitted Manchester United’s 1-1 draw with Tottenham Hotspur was a painful result, after his side failed to protect the lead against 10-man Tottenham at Old Trafford.

Manchester United looked set to claim three points when Bryan Mbeumo scored in the second half off Cunha’s low cross, but Dominic Solanke’s late equaliser in injury time left Carrick facing more questions on United’s performance and his future.

Speaking to BBC Match of the Day, the United manager felt his players improved after the break but failed to handle the situation when victory was within reach.

“It was a mixed game. We found it tough to start with. For a number of reasons, we were not quite there. You could see it was a challenging time,” Carrick said.

“But the lads grew into the game, in the second half I thought we were better in everything. To get the game as we wanted it, in such a good position – we should see it through. We have to manage those situations.”

United have now conceded two late goals that have cost them valuable points, something Carrick believes has made their position look worse than it might have otherwise.

Asked whether a lack of confidence had contributed to United’s slow start, he disagreed but admitted matches can quickly slip away from his side.

The boos at half-time and full-time also clearly affected him.

“It’s not nice, it hurts a lot because I care about this club. But I understand the disappointment, the reality is what it is, we need to get back to winning games.”
